# **[How Everyday Investors Are Building Weekly Income Without Chasing Stocks](https://substack.com/redirect/4f13e75c-2e85-4b9b-a9a1-9d7f91329d28?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4f13e75c-2e85-4b9b-a9a1-9d7f91329d28?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I remember watching investors in 2008 hold their breath...Waiting for their portfolios to recover. Some never did.
Today, markets still swing wildly. Headlines change by the hour. And most retirement accounts are built on one hope:
"Eventually, it'll go back up."
But what if retirement wasn't about waiting? What if it was about building income?
Over the past 20+ years, I've refined a structured approach designed to pursue **consistent weekly cash flow** using options -- without day trading, without gambling, and without needing a massive account.
Inside my Free Guidebook, you'll discover:
• Why most investors focus on growth -- and ignore income

• How weekly options can be used strategically instead of speculatively

• A repeatable framework built around rules, risk control, and structure

• How many everyday investors aim for $500-$5,000 per month in supplemental income
You can't control the market. But you can control your strategy.
[Learn More Here](https://substack.com/redirect/4f13e75c-2e85-4b9b-a9a1-9d7f91329d28?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
The most common criticism of the Cook years was that Apple became more iterative than innovative. Jobs gave the world the iPhone and the iPad. Cook gave the world better iPhones and bigger iPads. The one genuinely revolutionary product launched under Cook was the Apple Vision Pro. It was ambitious, expensive, and ahead of its time -- and it has not been the commercial success many hoped for. That single miss has often been used to paint the entire Cook era as lacking the spark that defined the Jobs years.
But that critique misses something important.
Cook never tried to be Steve Jobs because he never would be. He understood his job was different. His task was to protect and grow the extraordinary company Jobs left behind, not to chase the same kind of lightning-in-a-bottle breakthroughs that defined the previous decade because that was always going to be a losing game. In that respect, Cook succeeded remarkably well. He steered Apple through choppy waters -- new iPhone cycles, shifting consumer expectations, and a complete transformation in how people use technology -- **[while keeping the company highly profitable and the brand loyalty intact.](https://substack.com/redirect/fcf9c730-5ffc-4a4b-b809-af11f5148471?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** A record that is enviable in Silicon Valley given the tumultuous changes in the last 15 years.
Product changes were for the most part logical, decisions (like picking up Dr Dre's Beats headphone brand) were smart. The products that Cook brought to market were significant even if they weren't iPod-esque in their fanfare and pop culture impact. Look at your wrist, if you have an Apple watch or personal fitness tracker, Tim Cook was who made that happen with the launch of the Apple Watch in 2014. Accounts differ as to if Jobs had a hand in the Watch concept before his death but its launch and the rise of wearable tech is almost entirely Cook's doing.
Perhaps Cook's smartest strategic decision while at Apple will be the one that has yet to bear fruit. He chose not to dive headfirst into the billion-dollar AI arms race. While other tech giants poured hundreds of their billions into building their own massive AI models from scratch, Cook chose a different path. After a dismal attempt at dipping their toe into the AI space Apple chose to partner with proven players like OpenAI and Anthropic and Grok, bringing 3rd party AI apps to the iPhone and iPad, integrating their technology into the Apple ecosystem rather than shouldering the enormous costs and risks. **[Some critics have argued that this may be have been a misstep,](https://substack.com/redirect/96c6eb1e-74fc-4578-a51b-912bae2cc701?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** but there's no denying that as a result of his decision, Apple is not saddled with the kind of debt and infrastructure burden now weighing on companies like OpenAI, Meta and Oracle. Apple as a company is still truly cash rich, in a way that is fast becoming rare in this age of AI. That restraint may prove to be one of Cook's most lasting contributions When one day "Apple AI" (or what ever it is called) launches in the future and (probably) blows the competition away, it will likely owe its genesis to the decision that Cook made.

* * *
* * *
Now the torch **[passes to John Ternus](https://substack.com/redirect/a4c5bc94-ec5a-4dd3-8c2f-2b7fedd81734?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , who **[comes from a hardware background at Apple.](https://substack.com/redirect/bca9ca3f-28c4-4a8c-9b14-382fb0b7aa1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** That is a meaningful and a notable shift. Cook rose through the operations and supply chain side of the business. Ternus has spent his career deep in product development. Many observers hope this will bring **[a more product-focused approach in the years ahead](https://substack.com/redirect/b646825e-a775-45cf-a1f1-f1402217da5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** -- a return to the kind of hardware innovation that defined Apple at its Jobsian peak.
On balance, given the impossibly high bar set by Steve Jobs' passing, Tim Cook did exactly what he was supposed to do. He kept the company highly profitable. He made the smart, steady decisions. He preserved the brand loyalty that makes Apple one of the most valuable companies in the world to this day. He hand-picked a successor who can carry forward the legacy and above all, he never tried to be Steve Jobs.
In those respects, Tim Cook did a very good job.
The critics who said no one could follow Jobs were right about one thing -- it was an _**almost**_ impossible task. Cook proved that it was not an impossible one. He didn't try to recreate the magic. He simply kept the lights on, the profits flowing, and the brand strong during an era of enormous change.
That may not sound as glamorous as launching the iPhone, but in the real world of business, it is an achievement well worth respecting.

Perhaps Cook's smartest strategic decision while at Apple will be the one that has yet to bear fruit. He chose not to dive headfirst into the billion-dollar AI arms race. While other tech giants poured hundreds of their billions into building their own massive AI models from scratch, Cook chose a different path. After a dismal attempt at dipping their toe into the AI space Apple chose to partner with proven players like OpenAI and Anthropic and Grok, bringing 3rd party AI apps to the iPhone and iPad, integrating their technology into the Apple ecosystem rather than shouldering the enormous costs and risks. but there's no denying that as a result of his decision, Apple is not saddled with the kind of debt and infrastructure burden now weighing on companies like OpenAI, Meta and Oracle. Apple as a company is still truly cash rich, in a way that is fast becoming rare in this age of AI. That restraint may prove to be one of Cook's most lasting contributions When one day "Apple AI" (or what ever it is called) launches in the future and (probably) blows the competition away, it will likely owe its genesis to the decision that Cook made. Subscribe to defeat the mainstream media, promote capitalism and American exceptionalism. Now the torch , who That is a meaningful and a notable shift. Cook rose through the operations and supply chain side of the business. Ternus has spent his career deep in product development. Many observers hope this will bring -- a return to the kind of hardware innovation that defined Apple at its Jobsian peak. On balance, given the impossibly high bar set by Steve Jobs' passing, Tim Cook did exactly what he was supposed to do. He kept the company highly profitable. He made the smart, steady decisions. He preserved the brand loyalty that makes Apple one of the most valuable companies in the world to this day. He hand-picked a successor who can carry forward the legacy and above all, he never tried to be Steve Jobs. In those respects, Tim Cook did a very good job. The critics who said no one could follow Jobs were right about one thing -- it was an almost impossible task. Cook proved that it was not an impossible one. He didn't try to recreate the magic. He simply kept the lights on, the profits flowing, and the brand strong during an era of enormous change. That may not sound as glamorous as launching the iPhone, but in the real world of business, it is an achievement well worth respecting. | | As a proud Oregonian, I have a deep, unwavering appreciation for the natural beauty of our state and the endless outdoor spaces and opportunities it has to offer. **That's why this Earth Day, I'm as committed as ever to protecting our great state's clean air, water, and land for future generations.** **[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129963252/616151301/-2044921950?refcode=2026-04-22-earth&recurring=&amount=3&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=3464419c-713e-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDEvMS84OTQxMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNDY0NDE5Yy03MTNlLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=mV-nuBuK0Byn41WXtcAkL_qTm_sDXUnbFWH-wE3jvQI=)** To preserve Oregon's rivers, mountains, coasts, and valleys, _all_ of us must be a part of a greater movement to save our planet. We must tackle the climate crisis by moving toward a clean energy future. But today – the 56th annual Earth Day – that future is deeply uncertain. Earlier this year, Trump's EPA took two drastic steps to impede the fight against climate change. It will consider only the impact on industry when regulating pollution, and no longer the value of lives saved. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129963257/616151310/-2044921950?refcode=2026-04-22-earth&recurring=&amount=3&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=3464419c-713e-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDEvMS84OTQxMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNDY0NDE5Yy03MTNlLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=mV-nuBuK0Byn41WXtcAkL_qTm_sDXUnbFWH-wE3jvQI=) Then, the EPA rescinded what's been known as the "endangerment finding." clean_body: | | | | As a proud Oregonian, I have a deep, unwavering appreciation for the natural beauty of our state and the endless outdoor spaces and opportunities it has to offer. That's why this Earth Day, I'm as committed as ever to protecting our great state's clean air, water, and land for future generations. = To preserve Oregon's rivers, mountains, coasts, and valleys, all of us must be a part of a greater movement to save our planet. We must tackle the climate crisis by moving toward a clean energy future. But today – the 56th annual Earth Day – that future is deeply uncertain. Earlier this year, Trump's EPA took two drastic steps to impede the fight against climate change. It will consider only the impact on industry when regulating pollution, and no longer the value of lives saved. = Then, the EPA rescinded what's been known as the "endangerment finding." The endangerment finding, which was finalized in 2009, is the bedrock scientific determination underpinning the EPA's ability to regulate greenhouse gas emissions. | | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

| | On this Earth Day, we can celebrate our beautiful Earth and all of its natural wonders, but we must also still sound the alarm. **We still have a LOT of work to do to take on the climate crisis, and Trump and his Cabinet of fossil-fuel cronies are hellbent on taking us backward as fast as they can.** We need to end the world's addiction to fossil fuels. We are flooding the world with dangerous, planet-warming carbon dioxide and other gases from burning fossil fuels. But Trump, to fulfill a promise to oil and gas companies who donated to his campaign, is prioritizing oil and gas projects that are making this problem worse every day. The Earth is crying out for help — every year, we see oceans warming, snowpack declining, and increasingly intense natural disasters like wildfires and hurricanes. **We need action, and we need it now. And that's why I will always use every tool I have — from legislation to oversight to appropriations to speaking out — to ensure a sustainable future for generations to come.** So, on Earth Day, let's rededicate ourselves to a rapid and just transition to renewable energy and an end to the production of fossil fuels, and to educating America about the need to preserve our planet's precious biodiversity. Here's how you can help: make choices that reflect the future you believe in. Plant a tree, pick up litter, and make a plan to use less plastic. But don't stop there. clean_body: On this Earth Day, we can celebrate our beautiful Earth and all of its natural wonders, but we must also still sound the alarm. | | | | On this Earth Day, we can celebrate our beautiful Earth and all of its natural wonders, but we must also still sound the alarm. We still have a LOT of work to do to take on the climate crisis, and Trump and his Cabinet of fossil-fuel cronies are hellbent on taking us backward as fast as they can. We need to end the world's addiction to fossil fuels. We are flooding the world with dangerous, planet-warming carbon dioxide and other gases from burning fossil fuels. But Trump, to fulfill a promise to oil and gas companies who donated to his campaign, is prioritizing oil and gas projects that are making this problem worse every day. The Earth is crying out for help — every year, we see oceans warming, snowpack declining, and increasingly intense natural disasters like wildfires and hurricanes. We need action, and we need it now. And that's why I will always use every tool I have — from legislation to oversight to appropriations to speaking out — to ensure a sustainable future for generations to come. So, on Earth Day, let's rededicate ourselves to a rapid and just transition to renewable energy and an end to the production of fossil fuels, and to educating America about the need to preserve our planet's precious biodiversity. Here's how you can help: make choices that reflect the future you believe in. Plant a tree, pick up litter, and make a plan to use less plastic. But don't stop there. Join with others, organize, and push for bold change. A livable planet is within reach if we fight for it together. Onward! One thing that so inspires me about Sue’s approach to life and work is the question she asks herself every day: **“What am I going to do about it?”** (She even has it tattooed on her arm!) You can see Sue’s motto in her City Council record, particularly on climate issues. Take a look at all she’s accomplished in Providence over the past four years. **[Then — we need you to vote! clean_body: We need you to vote for your fave Sue action on Earth Day | | | Hi friends, Happy Earth Day! One thing that so inspires me about Sue’s approach to life and work is the question she asks herself every day: “What am I going to do about it?” (She even has it tattooed on her arm!) You can see Sue’s motto in her City Council record, particularly on climate issues. Take a look at all she’s accomplished in Providence over the past four years. | | #1 Carbon Neutral Buildings! 🏫🌍 Did you know that buildings account for over 70% of Providence’s carbon footprint? YIKES. That’s why Sue authored the Building Energy Reporting Ordinance and the Carbon Neutral Buildings Act — and got them passed unanimously on Council. The two new laws increase transparency about energy use and require that our local government buildings be powered by clean energy by 2040! | | | #2 Phasing Out Gas-Powered Leaf Blowers! 🍃⛽ This one is VERY popular! Sue introduced a new local law to phase out the use of gas-powered leaf blowers in Providence — one more small step toward keeping our air clean, clear, and safe for all! | | | #3 $3 Million Green Revolving Fund! 💚💸 Alongside Mayor Brett Smiley and Council President Rachel Miller, Sue announced a new $3 million revolving fund for local energy efficiency and clean energy projects. Even as the federal government retreats from clean energy, Providence is leading the way forward! | | It’s your turn to let us know: | Sue has been one of our community’s most dedicated climate and food policy advocates for a long time. # [Don't Put an Election Denier in Charge of the Fed](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tdafed0bf-8031-42b3-adcb-9da8cd4ef334/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)
---
| | [](https://default.salsalabs.org/Ta5634388-13ad-4f13-a575-2e7cc40dbe5e/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)
---
| | | Chairman of the Federal Reserve is one of the most important jobs in America, and arguably THE most important when it comes to the economy. **[Which is why we can’t have a nut job or an ass-kissing sock puppet in that position. And why the Senate must reject Trump’s nominee, Kevin Warsh.](https://default.salsalabs.org/T55891963-666c-4e87-aa9e-be05f7d90ac2/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)** Warsh appeared before the Senate Banking Committee to answer questions, and it was a disaster. The Fed Chair is supposed to make decisions independent of the White House, something especially critical when the person occupying the White House is a blithering idiot who is destroying the economy as we speak. Senator Elizabeth Warren attempted to test his independence by asking him very simple questions:

\- Did Donald Trump lose the 2020 election? - This is an easy softball, but he wouldn’t give a straight answer. He either believes Trump’s nonsense, or he’s too much of an ass-kisser to say anything out of sync with Trump.

\- Is there anything on which you disagree with Donald Trump? - Derp.

\- ANYTHING? Just one thing? - Homina, homina, homina

It really was cringe-worthy (watch [here](https://default.salsalabs.org/T78b2272d-9f62-418c-8f6a-b7b3d2e50d8e/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) and [here](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tdf879dad-564f-4f77-98ff-6a3f9c6fffce/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)). If Warsh is too scared to take on Trump on such easy questions, it’s pretty clear that he’s going to be doing Trump’s bidding, regardless of how stupid it is, and how catastrophic it will be for the economy. **[Add your name: Tell the Senate to Reject Warsh](https://default.salsalabs.org/T46206e68-24be-4efb-9d2d-a93e6c151423/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)**

Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
ABC: House Republicans propose stricter voting requirements as Trump administration eyes the midterms [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=042226_1&amount=25]
Folks, we've been warning you about the SAVE Act since it was introduced, since it's a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote.
Well, there's a new champion in the " anti-voting legislation " category with the introduction of the Make Elections Great Again (MEGA) Act. The new bill goes far beyond even the SAVE Act, with the MEGA Act now being called " the most extreme voting restrictions ever proposed at the federal level ."
The name also tells you everything you need to know about the target audience for this bill. With Trump focused on re-litigating the 2020 election, this legislation would give him all the power he would need to take federal control of the upcoming midterms .
PITCH IN $35 RIGHT NOW TO STOP THE MEGA ACT ➜ [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=042226_1&amount=35]
While the SAVE Act focused almost exclusively on requiring voters to produce documentary proof of citizenship when registering, the MEGA Act is far more sweeping. It would:
* Impose a strict photo ID requirement to vote
* Create a centralized voter surveillance system in every state
* Mandate constant voter roll purges, gutting the “Motor Voter” law that expanded access to voter registration
* Bar states from counting ballots that arrive after Election Day
* Ban universal mail voting, in which states mail a ballot to all registered voters
* Bar the federal funding for voter registration by outside groups
* Unleash lawsuits against election officials
Estimates said the SAVE Act could disenfranchise up to 11 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities. The MEGA Act would be much, much worse.
Team, the consequences of a bill like this passing would be catastrophic for our democracy. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to stop the MEGA Act and other voter suppression bills from becoming law >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=042226_1&amount=35]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=042226_1&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=042226_1&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=042226_1&amount=50]
GIVE $100 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=042226_1&amount=100] GIVE $250 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=042226_1&amount=250] OTHER AMOUNT [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=042226_1&amount=35]
The scariest parts of the MEGA Act are how it goes after so much more than proof-of-citizenship at registration. States aren't mandated to provide ID to eligible citizens, but the MEGA Act would require citizens to show the right kind of ID every time they went to vote. This creates inequality, like in Texas, where you can vote with a hunting license ( which doesn't require proof of citizenship ) but you can't vote with a college photo ID.
This bill targets voter registration as well, demanding that eligible voters re-prove their citizenship every election, while also requiring states to " take affirmative steps... on an ongoing basis " every 30 days to check and verify their voter rolls. How would they check them? Using a nationwide federal database controlled by MAGA partisans, of course . And the bill calls for all these measures to be in place before we vote in November's general election.
“ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights said about the SAVE Act. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ”
His words ring even more true about the MEGA Act. This bill is nothing less than an all-out partisan assault on our fundamental right to vote . If made law, this bill would codify MAGA's power for decades to come, invalidating millions of eligible voters and ending our democracy for a generation or longer.
None of us can afford to sit on the sidelines, Team, and watch our fundamental right to vote die. Fight back against these cynical vote suppressors with $35 or whatever you can before it's too late >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=042226_1&amount=35]

| | **In Northwest Washington, Earth Day is every day.** Our district is one of the most scenic and diverse in the country. From rolling hills, stunning valleys, and beautiful landscapes along the Puget Sound and the Salish Sea to our diverse ecosystem that supports large migrations of shore birds, beloved salmon returns, and the iconic bald eagle. Northwest Washington is beloved by environmentalists and adventurers alike. On this Earth Day, I am proud to share that we have earned the endorsement of the League of Conservation Voters (LCV)! [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129966401/616160614/1596212816?refcode=2026-04-22-lcv&recurring=&amount=7&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=701e6a83-763e-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3MDFlNmE4My03NjNlLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=twIEhTGKgfXWhOEDHL8laN1qkRai_IaM9vQ9Y6WdF-w=) LCV is a powerful force in American environmental politics, leveraging its resources and communication efforts to promote a greener and more sustainable future. **I am honored to have their support as I run for re-election in Congress, and I am grateful for their work to keep places like Northwest Washington beautiful for future generations.** LCV takes a wide range of issues into account when endorsing a candidate, including: climate change, democracy, environmental and racial justice, energy, public health, worker protections, public lands, and wildlife conservation. Given their robust rubrics, having their support is even more meaningful. clean_body: In Northwest Washington, Earth Day is every day. | | | | In Northwest Washington, Earth Day is every day. Our district is one of the most scenic and diverse in the country. From rolling hills, stunning valleys, and beautiful landscapes along the Puget Sound and the Salish Sea to our diverse ecosystem that supports large migrations of shore birds, beloved salmon returns, and the iconic bald eagle. Northwest Washington is beloved by environmentalists and adventurers alike. On this Earth Day, I am proud to share that we have earned the endorsement of the League of Conservation Voters (LCV)! = LCV is a powerful force in American environmental politics, leveraging its resources and communication efforts to promote a greener and more sustainable future. I am honored to have their support as I run for re-election in Congress, and I am grateful for their work to keep places like Northwest Washington beautiful for future generations. LCV takes a wide range of issues into account when endorsing a candidate, including: climate change, democracy, environmental and racial justice, energy, public health, worker protections, public lands, and wildlife conservation. Given their robust rubrics, having their support is even more meaningful. As we deal with warmer temperatures, rising sea levels, and climate-caused disasters, I will continue working to ensure our infrastructure can handle the changing climate and keep our communities safe. | | Peter,
---
I'm going to be blunt with you.

We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit.

Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way."

Right now.

And the scariest part?

It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms.

High schools. Colleges.

Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped.

If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: _" What happened to this country?" _

You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly.

Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything...

The other side is doing something far more dangerous.

They're raising the next generation.

Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places.

That's how countries are lost.

Slowly. Then all at once.

But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope...

There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged.

_And it shouldn 't even exist. _

**Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.**
That alone felt like a miracle.

Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have.

Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down.

And yet...

_They stepped up anyway. _

About that time, Charlie called me.

He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent.

"Andrew, we've got to move faster."

I told him we were. He stopped me.

"No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I actually laughed.

"Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said. "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000."

I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools.

We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet.

But Charlie wasn't fazed.

_" We'll figure it out." _

That was him.

He didn't wait for perfect conditions.

Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... _we lose everything. _

And now?

Less than a year later...

**We 're in 3,300 schools. **

**Thirteen percent of all high schools in America. **

**Eight states are now backing this effort to put a Club America chapter in every high school statewide. **

_That shouldn 't be possible. _

Not in this environment. Not with the level of hostility these students face every single day.

And yet... it's still happening.

_But Peter, here 's the part you need to understand: _

This is not a victory. It's a foothold.

_Because in the other 87% of schools? _

There is no resistance. None.

Just one-sided propaganda from the Left.

One-sided pressure on kids who are too young to even realize what's happening to them.

That's the reality.

The question isn't whether we're fighting. We are.

The question is whether it's enough.

Because right now, the students stepping up through Club America...

They're not the majority. _They 're the exception. _

They're the ones willing to take the heat.

The ones willing to stand alone.

The ones willing to risk being targeted just to say: _" I love this country." _

And every time one of those students raises their hand...

We have a choice.

Back them. _Or leave them on their own. _

**Because when a student starts a chapter, we send them an activism kit -- with American flags. Pocket Constitutions. Leadership tools. **

Everything they need to actually stand their ground.

Not symbolically. For real.

They've already made the decision to lead.

All they're waiting on... is you and me.

**Each activism kit costs $25. That 's it. **

$25 to make sure one student doesn't have to stand alone against the Left in a hostile school.

$25 to put real tools in their hands.

$25 to push back -- even if it's one campus at a time.

But here's what gives me hope, Peter...

Club America isn't slowing down. It's accelerating.

Because every day, more students are stepping forward.

Not because it's easy or popular...

_But because they know what 's at stake. _

They're starting chapters in schools where they were told not to.

They're speaking truth in classrooms where the Left once went unchallenged.

They're choosing courage in places designed to make them conform.

And they're not alone.

They're finding each other. They're bringing more students with them every day.

They're building something real -- rooted in faith and freedom, grounded in truth, and unafraid to say that America is worth defending.

That's how movements are built.

Not from the top down... _But from the ground up. _

One student. One school. One chapter at a time.

And Peter -- that's exactly how we take this country back.

But only if we move fast enough.

Because the Left isn't slowing down. They're not taking a break.

They're not afraid to push their anti-American ideas in every classroom they're in.

And if we don't match that urgency... if we don't meet that moment with equal conviction...

Then the generational window Charlie Kirk opened to save our country closes.

Not "if things keep going this way." Right now. And the scariest part? It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms. High schools. Colleges. Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped. If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: " What happened to this country?" You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly. Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything... The other side is doing something far more dangerous. They're raising the next generation. Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places. That's how countries are lost. Slowly. Then all at once. But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope... There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged. And it shouldn 't even exist. Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools. That alone felt like a miracle. Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have. Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down. And yet... They stepped up anyway. About that time, Charlie called me. He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent. "Andrew, we've got to move faster." I told him we were. He stopped me. "No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. body:
This weekend, I went on MS NOW to speak out about something that should
concern all of us. In an attempt to cast doubt on our elections, Trump’s
Department of Justice is demanding that Wayne County turn over all of the
2024 ballots.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/4278?t=1001&akid=1603%2E181023%2EGC-Tyz ]Jocelyn Benson on MS NOW.

As Secretary of State, I’ve spent years making sure our elections are
secure, fair, and accessible. We welcome scrutiny, we welcome observers —
but what we will not accept is intimidation, misinformation, or attempts
to undermine the will of the voters.

These new efforts from the Trump Administration are designed to sow doubt,
make people question results, lose faith in the process, and ultimately
disengage from our democracy altogether.

When Donald Trump and his allies tried to overturn the 2020 election, it
started with false claims about places like Detroit. Now, we’re seeing
similar tactics used again, but this time with an eye toward future
elections.

I want you to know that we will fight this, we will win in court, and we
will continue to defend the right of every Michigan citizen to have their
voice heard.

But this moment is also a reminder of why this race for governor matters
so much.

Because protecting our elections — and our democracy — requires leaders
who are willing to stand up, speak out, and never back down, no matter the
pressure.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/4278?t=1002&akid=1603%2E181023%2EGC-Tyz ]That’s exactly what I’ve done, and it’s exactly how I’ll continue to
lead. If you’re with me in this fight, can you chip in $25 or more today
to help us keep building this campaign?

Friend, It’s Earth Day today! I’m proud that our 2026 re-election campaign has already received endorsements from the Sierra Club and Sunrise Movement, and I will never stop fighting for environmental justice. **Today I want to lift up the legislation that I just re-introduced with Congresswoman Debbie Dingell: the**** _Water Access and Affordability Act_****.** We all deserve safe, accessible, and affordable drinking water: Water is life and we cannot live without it. But millions of our neighbors across the country can’t afford rising water bills and are facing water shutoffs. **If passed, our bill will ban inhumane water shutoffs and create the first-ever permanent federal water affordability program** at the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)—to help low-income families with the costs of water payments, debt relief, reconnection to water, water efficiency upgrades, and plumbing repairs. Each data center steals millions of gallons of water every day, and many also contaminate drinking water—sometimes leading to increased rates of cancer near data centers. They’re also polluting our air, contributing to climate change by increasing our reliance on fossil fuels, and delaying the needed transition to renewable energy.

Peter, I’m
fighting to build a government that focuses on improving lives, not ending
them.

That shouldn’t be a hot take. But looking at Donald Trump’s 2027 budget
proposal — and the years leading up to it — it is:

[ A ]A graph by @stephensemler showing US budgets less for improving lives,
more for ending them. The graph shows a gradual rise in war investments
and steep drop in public investment.

Trump wants $1.5 trillion for war. At the same time, he’s slashing funding
for public health, education, and the basic services that help working
people afford housing and food.

Our government shouldn’t be in the business of ending lives. But for
corporate PACs that profit from weapons sales, endless war is good
business — one that only the richest of the rich benefit from.

I’m running to change that.

Peter, I’m the
only candidate in this race who’s never taken a dime from corporate PACs,
and never will, so you know I’m fighting for us. And I won’t stop until
our tax dollars are invested in improving life here at home, not fueling
endless war overseas.

people-powered campaign is relying on grassroots donations to take on the
corrupt politics that brought us to this moment.

In solidarity,

Abdul

subject: STATEMENT: Virginians vote YES, reshape the fight for the U.S. House
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Virginians for Fair Elections
body:
# [](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/629?refcode=em20260422-558&t=1&akid=558%2E12592%2Eryow6V)
Last night, Virginia voters chose to fight back against Trump's effort to rig congressional maps ahead of the 2026 midterms.
In a special election with a single question and no statewide candidates on the ballot, millions of Virginians showed up — at levels that rival a general election — to defend fair representation. That is a remarkable statement about what was at stake.
The impact is immediate. The new maps, passed by the General Assembly and signed by Governor Spanberger, will now be in effect. At a moment when Donald Trump directed Republican legislatures across the country to redraw their maps to lock in a House majority before voters had their say, Virginia just changed the battlefield. The path to retaking the U.S. House of Representatives is fundamentally different tonight because Virginians chose to act.
This campaign was built in just five months — overcoming nearly $40 million spent on spreading MAGA lies and misinformation to confuse voters, navigating unprecedented legal challenges to stop Virginians from having a say, and asking voters to grapple with a complex issue for our democracy. But in the end, voters cut through the noise, made their voices heard, and voted YES.
We are deeply grateful to every Virginian who voted, volunteered, donated, and stood up in this moment. This victory belongs to them.
— Kéren Charles Dongo
Campaign Manager, Virginians for Fair Elections

body:
Please join me for my upcoming fundraiser!

| | | | |

| | | | [|

| | Friend,
I wanted to reach out again in case you missed my previous email inviting you to my upcoming fundraiser. **Your help is crucial to helping us flip this seat** ; I would love to have you join us for what should be a fantastic event! Please see below for the original invitation. —
In keeping with our promise to put the FUN back in FUNdraiser...**I’d like to personally invite you to join me on Saturday, May 9th for a day of trap shooting, great food, and even better company at the Medford Gun Club.**
This will be one of our last opportunities to come together before the May 19th Primary Election Day—and I can’t think of a better way to do it than breaking a few clays and sharing some laughs.
Your attendance—and your support—make a real difference. With your help, we will be able to reach voters, flip this seat, and bring the ABC’s -Affordability, Balance, and Common sense - back to Salem.
👉 **Please RSVP by May 1st by making your donation below**.
Space is limited, and I’d hate for you to miss your shot. Each ticket comes with one shooting slot, lunch for yourself, and lunch for one non-shooting guest.
If you’d prefer to pay by check, just reach out to debra@hicksforsenate.com and we’ll get you squared away.
**Whether you’re a seasoned shooter or just there for the BBQ, I hope you’ll join us...and possibly some surprise special guests!**
I look forward to seeing you on May 9th.******-**_**Brad Hicks**_

But Derek, those plans quickly fizzled out. I was cut from my college basketball team, and nearly flunked out of organic chemistry... on the same day. It wasn’t until someone knocked on my dorm room door and asked if I wanted to run for student government, I began to seriously think about elected office. And when I won? I saw exactly what dependable, commonsense leadership could accomplish. During my year as Student Association president, I was laser-focused on safety. We added more outdoor lights, blue light security phones, and even improved our shuttle service at night. Seeing my work make a real difference in folks’ lives — it was an amazing feeling, Derek. And I’ve been doing the same ever since. Working hard to make sure folks can be safe and feel safe in their communities, putting more money in families’ pockets, bringing Pennsylvanians together, and protecting your Constitutional freedoms from those who want to sabotage them. Look, I know politics gets a bad rap — and a lot of the time, it’s justified. But I saw it in college, and I’m seeing it today as your Governor: **Good things happen when leaders are focused on delivering for others.** I’m damn proud of everything we’ve accomplished together, Derek. But I’m not naive: The far-right has piles of cash stashed away to boost a candidate who is focused on appeasing Donald Trump – and not the good people of Pennsylvania. So today, I’m humbly asking: [_**Will you chip in a donation of any amount to help us stay on track for victory here in Pennsylvania? ---
| | Friend,
---
I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground.

Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible.
---
[](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=a7dda469126d43aab50664c8d18cc54f&_e=1EMzknIMV1jtXyCUJG5_IMevCF34Ad3x-QyAZ9-ZTNcJ_hGYNjIMjfWupfDnlo5WZbwXF9CnStQKhB38cFOHWFYCgklj4QClJsxlMHibeEs8-5ISbI2krmG5Aqhf3ptEQAfmL5NI1zNzLrvuljUi0_E7ThDLLR8QuMbdfN6Z04ZQBLx1KPAqbRa23XIfRGlqx96tSX8AlUML2qCwf9fjFZPUqO40gaOU8p1EdMmkgNpcypu-VEHf9684KunBv3R95BubW8nOCeh6VORp1nxByyimfLrjnJTw_lep8ZZ2lNo6cbJdW4U35S9kAEv6wPmxxgrSbbrKuLCdghn4pY8NnSRfWfCRp35cmJWxcU9VqIfgFecIDwK5pAIYXR-0dLwdwvQqGaZy5gyK3cgNbW7mp8XAPgOFsJhx7eUvsYzSYROt_1xtCOMVYQUKsIbqaTi_oy_3fkCJgdI2HFq9VrAGlnLRVHvBjW1OXQBJmq_wGbJR5Q7op-8Cui3DC1W7hr35tUkYr4_sempLZtINqyqm0Ojc9p2D-NKncbSuPrAI-u2YpMNNnB3leUo6RsAsy0OXOdEbWJnEB-iZzu1-e86X7277kTgAVzDgZoLCmcAvlHR66aQWi2BrjFFywafSxsHTf3jkei1wW9m0tBd_E4LL-oOELOjgT9icz1mnEookySBfOsPmyJCq5m2tuoTUMG_9wEOWKZoeXbeARn87dH22eA%3D%3D)
---
_Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona_
---
These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

**We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. **

For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there.

And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet.
---
[](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=a7dda469126d43aab50664c8d18cc54f&_e=1EMzknIMV1jtXyCUJG5_IMevCF34Ad3x-QyAZ9-ZTNcJ_hGYNjIMjfWupfDnlo5WZbwXF9CnStQKhB38cFOHWFYCgklj4QClJsxlMHibeEs8-5ISbI2krmG5Aqhf3ptEQAfmL5NI1zNzLrvuljUi0_E7ThDLLR8QuMbdfN6Z04ZQBLx1KPAqbRa23XIfRGlqx96tSX8AlUML2qCwf9fjFZPUqO40gaOU8p1EdMmkgNpcypu-VEHf9684KunBv3R9tKlkKZDjt_xiWktxheY9OaeLA1U3zHBktWz39FHEpLKnk02FEA6wOj29IxEdwxm1mA1NxcgHyRfbWHwg4oU-2bgBxnr-eor3pxrAPQy0g7kUXKAA2e-HPlZLzvrlB0FcTA5bZnXfhcJyKUEi14SWzyRBJrGp03Tsn-7KWSNCNc9TXGEIHKO0iCmS_tz0KwerzBSeBoBMTgC18EoJnLih0Q9cfGIWvNBHQoK0z6qTq7BHWpIKWgJYrPMEysfev9MW9U1wC21hNQ4psuHbcxvyT9mUsTBlLH2tPvkyoEW-yXVkhAY_xJ8RG8CCasFZK4vWeJ15yj3HY_P20PnVuQX7MKgyW3LY0hmyuhSW-cOuRzpv0Ad6PVWCyz7DDBz-CmENC0hjWrUJPtk5wOdkonaoVQlNSpZ9H7U-BuKRYBDm1xOVxmv-TwxiMM9qv9UsOodKV0SmZ8qz9zlklgryJKDX_A%3D%3D)
---
That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens.

And it's not isolated growth anymore.

**We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. **

But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America.

That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation...

And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak.

So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build.

What's different now is the pace.

**Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: **

✅ Arkansas
✅ Florida
✅ Idaho
✅ Indiana
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Oklahoma
✅ South Carolina
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee

That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action.
---
[](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=a7dda469126d43aab50664c8d18cc54f&_e=1EMzknIMV1jtXyCUJG5_IMevCF34Ad3x-QyAZ9-ZTNcJ_hGYNjIMjfWupfDnlo5WZbwXF9CnStQKhB38cFOHWFYCgklj4QClJsxlMHibeEs8-5ISbI2krmG5Aqhf3ptEQAfmL5NI1zNzLrvuljUi0_E7ThDLLR8QuMbdfN6Z04ZQBLx1KPAqbRa23XIfRGlqx96tSX8AlUML2qCwf9fjFZPUqO40gaOU8p1EdMmkgNpcypu-VEHf9684KunBv3R9cL8Hr1uNuQBPUt3RR8IKm1LDbSFCXRqVEqZH18cXLLIC9dflawOw4A9t_EvM0qIG21qjvmF7hVO71qfbNQMcU551n83t5fU97Cpg4KleoVXPbAk7zNdO85RRgUURmsTSBSwI-TqqN0h81pBLNfdsoLWg1KZbbeX869dEfT8RnSifvMFIhAU0PkAI-lfsOkqbi2K4yr9V5yJKHSQvWCi8ZDXnpW8lgwxOX2fYcRe_cJs9AlbvwuwUMlK_qHMeGGxcWQU1MnvYYBIpf6SqpX0Z2i0NLh-WmVq_TV_wpK2dFDZiExaOuG9fh_X3IHFKinbRwStMhxi6lAhX7HzDfnQ3TU3SIgzdHzWGtKeUDTheIemUQO5F58WLYHfmqEEg8mHZr4FJ87Okixbgo5pYHDv9_n8koC756itfZQLTlH_S4kU55vtyMjQT-gYkMdsZb_o9eKGFyjxRb5Dy45GEICkfCg%3D%3D)
---
That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly.

It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up.

Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through.

And right now, that's where we're stretched.

We're not lacking interest or momentum.

We're working to keep up with both.

_So here 's how you can help... _

Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it.

**An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: **

✅ Constitutions.
✅ Chapter guides.
✅ Flags.
✅ Materials to organize and lead.

It turns a student who wants to speak up... _into one who actually does. _

body:
Sunrise Movement knows that a brighter future for all is worth fighting for
#
When Alexandria first introduced the Green New Deal — a resolution to address the worsening climate crisis by creating millions of good, union jobs to end our dependence on fossil fuels — naysayers immediately called it ‘unrealistic.’
But **Sunrise Movement knows that a brighter future for all is worth fighting for**.
They are laser-focused on building a youth movement to crack the grip of fossil fuels on our politics and prove that climate policy can actually improve the lives of everyday people across the country.
The cynics want us to think that the climate crisis is insurmountable.
But Sunrise knows: we can win a better future and a liveable planet because of the commitment of every single person demanding change.
[This Earth Day, join us in support of the next generation fighting for our future by making a contribution to Sunrise Movement. Hi there, friend – Michael Bennet here.
After spending almost 17 years fighting for Colorado’s working families in the Senate, I often get asked why I’m running for governor. The answer is simpler than you might think:
Right now, GOP majorities in Congress are letting Trump’s chaos, corruption and cruelty run wild. They’re failing to rein in the massive corporations hiking prices and lowering our quality of life.
Meanwhile, Trump’s revenge campaign against blue states has left Colorado hanging out to dry.
So right now, I’m running to take the fight for Colorado’s working families where I can make the biggest possible impact: **here in our home state.**
**_[That's why I'm asking you to donate $5, split between Jacky Rosen and myself, toward my campaign's $100,000 public reporting goal (our biggest one yet)](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129973550/616183026/-1546580899?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=jtk5765-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNTZhNWU4ZS04NjNlLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=3AhVlKhpY7t67Q87jBiqD2vcG1x7OJ2d6SJpjBbJphM=)_** – because Colorado deserves a leader who will unite folks to tackle our biggest challenges and deliver real change.
I'm the only guy with the hands-on experience and the values and bold vision to lead our state out of Trump’s second Gilded Age.
I’m also the _only_ one with tangible plans to improve Coloradans' lives, like:
* Cutting red tape to build more starter homes and affordable housing options

* Creating a Colorado Public Option to expand affordable health care access

* Launching a Cap and Invest program to cut emissions and utility bills

* Raising teacher pay and ensuring every high school graduate can make a living wage, and more.

That’s what it takes to build a future where working families can spend less than 30% of their paycheck on housing, join the middle class, and thrive. We already have all the tools here in our home state to get this to-do list done. We just need the right leader in the governor's office.
**_That's_ why I'm in this race and why Politico’s called my campaign the frontrunner to win since launch day.**
But April 29 is our only public reporting deadline before the primary election. As soon as our numbers go public, everyone will be looking to see whether we have the grassroots strength to stay in the lead. **I won't have the resources to win in November without a strong base of small-dollar grassroots support from everyday folks like you, friend.**
**[I’m committed to the work ahead, and I’d love it if you came along for the ride. So if you're in a place to give, I hope you'll consider splitting a contribution now between Jacky Rosen and myself ahead of our crucial reporting deadline.>>](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129973551/616183027/-1189732401?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&refcode=jtk5765-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNTZhNWU4ZS04NjNlLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=3AhVlKhpY7t67Q87jBiqD2vcG1x7OJ2d6SJpjBbJphM=)**

clean_body: | | | Hi there, friend – Michael Bennet here. After spending almost 17 years fighting for Colorado’s working families in the Senate, I often get asked why I’m running for governor. The answer is simpler than you might think: Right now, GOP majorities in Congress are letting Trump’s chaos, corruption and cruelty run wild. They’re failing to rein in the massive corporations hiking prices and lowering our quality of life. Meanwhile, Trump’s revenge campaign against blue states has left Colorado hanging out to dry. So right now, I’m running to take the fight for Colorado’s working families where I can make the biggest possible impact: here in our home state. = – because Colorado deserves a leader who will unite folks to tackle our biggest challenges and deliver real change. I'm the only guy with the hands-on experience and the values and bold vision to lead our state out of Trump’s second Gilded Age. I’m also the only one with tangible plans to improve Coloradans' lives, like: Cutting red tape to build more starter homes and affordable housing options Creating a Colorado Public Option to expand affordable health care access Launching a Cap and Invest program to cut emissions and utility bills Raising teacher pay and ensuring every high school graduate can make a living wage, and more. That’s what it takes to build a future where working families can spend less than 30% of their paycheck on housing, join the middle class, and thrive. We already have all the tools here in our home state to get this to-do list done. We just need the right leader in the governor's office. That's why I'm in this race and why Politico’s called my campaign the frontrunner to win since launch day. But April 29 is our only public reporting deadline before the primary election. As soon as our numbers go public, everyone will be looking to see whether we have the grassroots strength to stay in the lead. I won't have the resources to win in November without a strong base of small-dollar grassroots support from everyday folks like you, friend. = | | = Thank you for your consideration, Michael | *

Peter, Last night I took the debate stage at Southern University, and I wanted to reach out to all of my top supporters to let you know what we talked about.
I got asked a lot of policy questions. I gave detailed answers on healthcare, affordability, voting rights, and how we're going to fight corporate price gouging.
But the moment that mattered most to me came at the end, when I got to explain something I believe in my bones:
How the farmer standing before you wins this race, and makes history in Louisiana.
Because here's the truth: Democrats don't just need the right policies. We need a candidate who can deliver those policies to voters across Louisiana -- in cities, in suburbs, and in rural communities where we've been losing ground for years.
I'm a farmer from northeast Louisiana. I've spent my life working the same Delta soil my grandfather worked as a sharecropper -- except now my family owns it. I've served my community in local government. I've built a business. And I know how to talk to people who've stopped listening to Democrats because they don't think we understand their lives.
We win this race by meeting voters where they are, and making a compelling, personal case that the MAGA status quo is killing our state and our democracy.
And here's the thing: It's working. I've seen it out on the doors, in the polls, and in the results of special elections nationwide, including right here in Louisiana.
This is the cycle to make history and elect the first Black man to the Senate from Louisiana since Reconstruction.
And I firmly believe we're building the grassroots army necessary to tackle the MAGA army at the ballot box.

body:
Not what I spent my time doing

| | | | |
Peter,
I’ll be honest with you... I’m not great at asking for money. It’s the part of this job I hate the most.
I didn’t spend my twenties learning how to fundraise to run for office. I spent them flying H-46 helicopters for the Navy and deploying to the Persian Gulf.
And when I came home, I didn’t become a lobbyist who took clients out to expensive dinners. I used my GI Bill to become a Geriatric Nurse Practitioner. My "networking" was holding the hands of our seniors and listening to their stories, not cutting backroom deals.
That’s really who I am...a Helicopter Pilot...a Nurse Practitioner... and a Mom trying to raise four happy and healthy kids in a world that feels like it’s going in the wrong direction most days.
[I didn't run for Congress for the title. I ran because I looked at the country my children were inheriting, and I felt sick to my stomach. **" Texas economy hits $2.9 trillion. Here's what that means"** via [Austin American-Statesman](https://substack.com/redirect/0d5b2d49-208c-4afd-a88a-373de57e9576?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Dante Motley** - Texas is celebrating a new bragging-rights number: $2.9 trillion. That figure, highlighted in a Friday announcement from Gov. Greg Abbott, is the state's preliminary 2025 current-dollar gross domestic product, based on estimates from the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis.

"With the Best Business Climate in America and unmatched pro-growth policies, Texas is the premier destination for job creators from across the country and world," Abbott said. "We will keep attracting world-class investment, create jobs, and expand opportunity for Texans for generations to come." So what is Texas really claiming here?

The state produced about $2.9 trillion worth of goods and services in 2025, and its economy grew faster than the nation as a whole in real, inflation-adjusted terms, according to the governor's office. GDP is the broadest scoreboard for the size of an economy. It tries to capture the value created across industries, from oilfields and chip plants to hospitals, law firms, warehouses and restaurants.

When the governor's office says Texas hit $2.9 trillion, it is pointing to the BEA's estimate for the value of all that activity in 2025. The "current-dollar" part means the number is not scrubbed of inflation. Prices rising can help push the total up, even when the economy is not booming in the way everyday people might imagine. _([AAS](https://substack.com/redirect/0d5b2d49-208c-4afd-a88a-373de57e9576?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Demand tsunami: Energy leaders foresee exponential need as Texas economy expands"** via [Fort Worth Report](https://substack.com/redirect/47bc33f0-3a1c-46e6-a238-05a3772e3cbf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Bob Francis** and **Eric E. Garcia** - Driven by economic growth, data centers and an increasingly urban population, industry leaders in Texas foresee energy demand increasing exponentially over the next decade.

"We've had this relatively flat growth for the last two decades," said **Tony Robinson** , president and CEO of nuclear power company Framatome. "That's changed, and I think we're using the wrong term. I don't think it's a surge in demand. I think it's a tsunami."

Robinson cited the amount of power needed by data centers, for cloud computing and crypto mining, the state's growing population along with all the electronic devices used by consumers as major contributions to this increase in energy needs.

"The amount needed on a daily basis is astronomical," he said. _([Fort Worth Report](https://substack.com/redirect/47bc33f0-3a1c-46e6-a238-05a3772e3cbf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" UT announces new Dell Medical Center, research campus after $750 million gift"** via [Texas Public Radio](https://substack.com/redirect/3efa1272-5b06-4b96-925f-105cdd170564?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Olivia Aldridge** - After a historic $750 million gift from the **Michael** &**Susan Dell** Foundation, The University of Texas at Austin's future hospital has a name: The UT Dell Medical Center. It will be part of the newly announced UT Dell Campus for Advanced Research, which will focus on clinical care and research in combination with advanced computing and artificial intelligence.

At a press conference Tuesday, the Dells, along with state and university officials, emphasized the opportunity to build a world-class university medical center that integrates modern technology from the ground up.

"By bringing together medicine, science and computing in one campus designed for the AI era, UT can create more opportunity, deliver better outcomes, and build a stronger future for communities across Texas and beyond," said Michael and Susan Dell in a news release.

The Dells' gift is one of the largest ever given to a United States university, and the couple are now the first donors to surpass $1 billion in lifetime giving to UT Austin. They were also integral in launching the university's medical school -- also named for the Dells -- with a $50 million donation in 2013. In addition to the new university hospital and research campus, the Dells' latest investment will also support undergraduate scholarships, student housing and UT's Texas Advanced Computing Center. _([TPR](https://substack.com/redirect/3efa1272-5b06-4b96-925f-105cdd170564?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" New World screwworm closer than ever to US, Texas ag secretary says"** via [KXAN](https://substack.com/redirect/11ce8dd8-478f-4b76-a863-6086cb8662ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Sandra Sanchez** \-- A calf infected with New World screwworm in the Mexican border state of Nuevo Leon is the closest reported case of the deadly parasite to the U.S. border, Texas Agriculture Secretary Sid Miller says. The case was just 62 miles from South Texas, Miller announced Monday.

"The threat of the New World screwworm is creeping dangerously close to our border," Miller said. "This is now the northernmost active case in Mexico, and that puts Texas squarely in the crosshairs."

The location of the calf is within the current sterile fly dispersal zone -- that's an area where the U.S. Department of Agriculture is releasing 100 million sterilized screwworm flies weekly to try to stop the deadly pest from crossing the border into the United States.

U.S. Agriculture Secretary **Brooke Rollins** on Friday visited Moore Air Base, outside Edinburg, from where planes fly the sterilized flies and drop them north and south of the border. The government is building a $610 million sterile fly facility on the base to eventually produce and release 300 million sterilized screwworm flies weekly from there. _([KXAN](https://substack.com/redirect/11ce8dd8-478f-4b76-a863-6086cb8662ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**2026**
**" What to know about the special election starting today in Southeast Texas"** via [San Antonio Express-News](https://substack.com/redirect/5c34f114-03d2-4339-8a9f-acdd0a015989?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s**Benjamin Wermund** - Voting is underway in the race to replace state Sen.**Brandon Creighton** , a Conroe Republican who vacated his seat in October after he was named chancellor of the Texas Tech University System. The district stretches from Port Arthur up to Montgomery County. The winner of the special election will serve the remainder of Creighton's term, which ends in January. Voters in November will decide who should fill the seat for a full four-year term.

Early voting runs through April 28. Election Day is May 2.

Republican **Brett Ligon** , who served as Montgomery County district attorney from 2008 to last year, is running with the backing of Creighton and Lt. Gov. **Dan Patrick** , who runs the Senate. Ligon has said property tax relief, border security and public safety are his top priorities. He faces Democrat **Ron Angeletti** , a special education advocate who is running for office for the first time. Angeletti has said his top priorities include public school funding and flood mitigation.

The deep-red district stretches north and east from Houston. It includes The Woodlands and Conroe to the north and runs east along I-10 between Baytown and Beaumont, neither of which are in the district's boundaries. It also includes Port Arthur. _([SAEN](https://substack.com/redirect/5c34f114-03d2-4339-8a9f-acdd0a015989?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Here are the biggest issues on the ballot in North Texas as early voting begins"** via [Dallas News](https://substack.com/redirect/d005bb11-4d30-409c-a7e8-05e0b31df311?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s**Lilly Kersh** - Whether Dallas Area Rapid Transit faces the end of the road in parts of North Texas heads to the ballot Monday, as early voting opens on DART membership in three cities and a slate of high-stakes issues. Here's what voters should know before heading to the polls.

Voters in Addison, University Park and Highland Park will decide whether they'll continue as part of DART or leave the region's public transportation system. Tensions between smaller, suburban member cities and the agency simmered to a boiling point last year. Local leaders decried the multimillion-dollar price tag of a one-cent sales tax they pay to DART for what some called inadequate services and minimal representation.

After the agency proposed a restructured governance and funding model, three cities called elections off. But DART's future in the Park Cities and Addison will still be determined at the ballot box. Addison residents can vote at any Dallas County Early Voting Center, including Addison Town Hall. Highland and University Park residents can vote early at University Park United Methodist Church. A full list of locations and hours for all three cities can be found at the Dallas County election website.

Residents will see a proposition on their ballots with the question: Shall the Dallas Area Rapid Transit System be continued in your town or city? With an option of 'yes' to keep DART or 'no' to leave the system. Service will stop in cities that leave DART the day after votes are canvassed. This official examination of the votes happens three to eleven days after the election. _([DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/d005bb11-4d30-409c-a7e8-05e0b31df311?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" San Antonio area voter guide: May 2 school board, bond and local municipal races"** via [Texas Public Radio](https://substack.com/redirect/27b38047-2688-40d0-92cb-fa3c9198f05e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - Deadlines are approaching for the May 2 local elections, when voters across the San Antonio area will weigh a range of community decisions. School board races lead the ballot, with other local contests that could shape schools, spending and city leadership.

Depending on where they live, registered voters may cast ballots in school board races and municipal contests. Learn about the races and candidates below, and scroll for information on when, where and how to vote.

Four candidates are vying to represent single-member district 9 in northeast Bexar County on the board of trustees for the Alamo Colleges. Elections for two other single-member districts were cancelled because no one filed to run against the incumbents. **Lorraine Pulido** and **Clint Kingsbury** have both been declared duly re-elected for another six-year term. Pulido represents District 4 on the southwest side, and Kingsbury represents District 8, which includes parts of north central Bexar County. _([TPR](https://substack.com/redirect/27b38047-2688-40d0-92cb-fa3c9198f05e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" James Talarico's $27M haul is huge -- but the GOP money machine looms large"** via [Houston Chronicle](https://substack.com/redirect/020887f9-ba4e-40b9-8813-fe66de48f122?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **John C. Moritz** - James Talarico's eye-popping $27 million fundraising haul may dominate early headlines, but it masks a deeper reality: Republicans still hold powerful financial advantages that could reshape the race once the general election begins. The report Talarico filed with the Federal Election Commission, made public Wednesday, shows he raised $27 million during the first three months of the year.

Incumbent Sen. **John Cornyn** , seeking his fifth term in Washington, collected about $9 million, and his GOP primary rival Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** 's haul was $2.2 million. The numbers suggest Talarico has seized early momentum. But candidate fundraising totals alone offer an incomplete picture. Political action committees, or PACs, and super PACs often play a decisive role in modern Senate campaigns.

Talarico's total was the highest among all Senate candidates nationwide and marked the most ever raised by a Senate candidate in the first quarter of an election year. He is not alone: Democrats in several competitive states are outraising Republicans. Incumbent Sen. **John Ossoff** of Georgia raised $13 million -- more than all three Republicans hoping to challenge him in the fall combined -- and similar patterns are emerging in North Carolina, New Hampshire, Alaska and elsewhere.

Yet the broader financial battlefield still tilts toward Republicans. The GOP's Senate Leadership Fund, which can distribute money to candidates nationwide, is sitting on a massive war chest. From Jan. 1 through March 31, the super PAC took in $72 million and reported $166 million in cash on hand. By comparison, the Democratic Senate Majority PAC raised $56 million during the same period and reported less than $75 million in the bank, or about half that of its Republican counterpart. That imbalance could prove decisive, particularly in a state as expensive as Texas. _([HOU CHRON](https://substack.com/redirect/020887f9-ba4e-40b9-8813-fe66de48f122?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Houston City Council approves revised immigration policy amid funding fight"** via KHOU's**Orko Manna** , **Jaime E. Galvan** and **Sammy Turner** -- Houston City Council on Wednesday approved a revised version of the city's controversial immigration ordinance, a decision that could determine the fate of roughly $114 million in public safety funding.

Councilmembers voted 13-4 on the measure after hours of debate and public input, with the revised language focused on how Houston police cooperate with federal immigration authorities.

Councilmember **Abbie Kamin** motioned to delay the vote by a week, but that motion was voted down.

The updated ordinance refines language around field encounters, ICE administrative warrants and reporting requirements for immigration-related policing.

It states that Houston police will comply with all local, state and federal laws and can temporarily detain someone for as long as reasonably necessary. It also makes clear that nothing in the policy prohibits cooperation with federal immigration authorities.

Mayor **John Whitmire 's** office has said the revised language creates a clearer path to restoring public safety funding that had been put at risk.

The vote comes after Texas Gov. **Greg Abbott** threatened to pull roughly $114 million in public safety funding if the city did not revise the ordinance.

City leaders say that funding supports a wide range of efforts, including police operations, domestic violence response, human trafficking investigations and homicide cases.

"They have the funds ... $114 million for HPD to carry out their duties," Whitmire said.

The city has also warned it does not have the resources to replace that funding if it is permanently lost. (_[KHOU](https://substack.com/redirect/56acae69-df41-4b44-9cef-d6eff5862b3f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Testing finds toxic metals where Tesla lithium refinery discharges wastewater in South Texas"** via Inside Climate News - After Texas regulators said Tesla's lithium refinery near Corpus Christi wasn't violating its permits by discharging what local officials reported as black wastewater into a drainage ditch, independent water testing there this month found two toxic metals and other contaminants.

Eurofins Environment Testing, an accredited lab with locations across the globe, reported traces of hexavalent chromium, a well-known carcinogen, and arsenic, an environmental poison. Nueces County Drainage District No. 2, which manages the ditch, commissioned the test.

Neither hexavalent chromium nor arsenic is included as an allowable discharge pollutant in Tesla's wastewater permit.

"The results are quite disturbing," wrote **Frank Lazarte** , an attorney representing Nueces County Drainage District No. 2, in a cease and desist letter to Tesla's associate general counsel last week. The district is asking Tesla to stop discharging wastewater into the ditch until they can discuss the lab results. _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/ab40f65a-7ecd-4d0d-9945-63f075f0eeda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_
