Friend,

When I turn on the TV or check my phone, all I hear is partisan chatter.

The clip economy is built to drive clicks and capture attention, but none of that actually helps a family afford childcare or a veteran connect with social services.

In Congress, I’ve found that the real work doesn’t happen on the front pages; it happens when we sit down at the table to solve the real problems that local families face. Whether I’m meeting with our families in Howard County or working with local organizations to protect the Chesapeake Bay, my focus is on delivering results for our families, not making speeches in D.C.

I’m not here to robotically vote “no” for two years or engage in petty squabbles. I’m in Washington to be part of the solution. Realistically, we won’t fix decades-old policy challenges in a single bill. We can’t deliver solutions if we’re not willing to attempt to find common ground with others. Still, every small win builds on the other until we finally move the needle and deliver tangible results that Maryland families deserve.

I’m laser-focused on these quiet wins that don’t make the front page.

Whether it’s securing an IRS refund for a neighbor, helping someone navigate the immigration system, or ensuring a veteran finally gets an appointment at the VA, my team and I are here to answer the phone and help you overcome even the smallest hurdle.

But this work — community roundtables, phone calling, and the nitty-gritty legislative work — is only possible because of your support.

If you believe in prioritizing local needs over partisan theatrics, could you contribute to my reelection campaign today? Peter, The New York Times just obtained a series of secret Supreme Court memos from 2016. **What they found had our jaws on the floor.** [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMdUS12fSrk6MMZIR1Ut2K6fzNFGLRHmgujr_IKbsEumaNtgSoUNzi2tORB9F0hjLvnPyr5Itx5Tc3vjSiipEyky-gCEVqAf9WN81VD3QLqKoYnpVYEvSob6VDUZgWC4VQANaT56pclPFQEpGIUchB1X5sk3zEP9YDVykD1k3LTjNL0rEgstXCTWow5oT24qAupVhcKCc_T1mUi1wNFbIYU4q6Cvs5OxrE_T-eoRlJ-HYyeOJFCUF5IYvoALR-sT2wSJLAkLNYxwhZ0PtgzrmpMKIHQYConAaRuZazMqqmRY3JZ6ARAN3LzKrBWoS49Fx6_NmXEVUTmQnD-VpakoJtoLgIvu5r3Op3kQg73iAL1IYSmuI_UEdqAgg5AHUX2NPjg/4q0/vcAkCalWSrKTMnDfeg1OgQ/h0/h001.ME2cMpAQCe21yEcknMWw6jOz9keO-FK2CMHm-cwrWIw) [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMdUS12fSrk6MMZIR1Ut2K6fzNFGLRHmgujr_IKbsEumaNtgSoUNzi2tORB9F0hjLvnPyr5Itx5Tc3vjSiipEyky-gCEVqAf9WN81VD3QLqKoYnpVYEvSob6VDUZgWC4VQANaT56pclPFQEpGIUchB1X5sk3zEP9YDVykD1k3LTjNL0rEgstXCTWow5oT24qAumLH09yNAs0oXq5G8VDdqc9vEhOI6DslZPofzIEFcHWogIk8-ZPubw53VPyPM-xI_O1LjD1Cs9JF882-mamgnNsKmn0tRBl9fCZvMti7KWqjsZpuwXuGAwNF6KDSrYkyKikT8zYwbF6Uaz_jVE3PIJ2QmEx5CTxKn7DqVZ1B9IZbVd8NHFlKk-n2ajc-5Oi8QA/4q0/vcAkCalWSrKTMnDfeg1OgQ/h1/h001.NTP0dfIeNqev_CwTU7kmomVOhK9WyQW4BFQSjH21zP0) In February of 2016, the Supreme Court broke from two centuries of tradition to inexplicably issue a cryptic, one-paragraph, last-minute ruling rather than a careful, deliberative decision informed by oral arguments. **Experts have pinpointed the moment as the birth of the “shadow docket,” the secretive, unilateral process that Chief Justice John Roberts and the MAGA justices have used to hand Trump dozens of victories.** In that case, the conservative justices rushed to block President Obama’s signature environmental policy. According to the uncovered memos, Chief Justice Roberts felt he needed to defend the energy industry from “the most expensive regulation ever imposed on the power sector.” The justices wrote back and forth between one another for five days. By the end of those 120 hours, the Obama initiative was dead—no other court had weighed in and no reasoning was given. **Even more consequential: the Court’s mode of operating had been fundamentally reshaped, just in time for the Trump era.** **Today the Supreme Court has repeatedly used the shadow docket to rule in Trump’s favor, supporting his attacks on immigration and civil rights and his attempts to expand executive power.** [**The memos uncovered by the New York Times paint a shocking picture of just how radically Chief Justice Roberts and the MAGA justices have transformed the Supreme Court and our justice system. We’re sharing the article far and wide so the American people can understand just how far the corruption goes.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMdUS12fSrk6MMZIR1Ut2K6fzNFGLRHmgujr_IKbsEumaNtgSoUNzi2tORB9F0hjLvnPyr5Itx5Tc3vjSiipEyky-gCEVqAf9WN81VD3QLqKoYnpVYEvSob6VDUZgWC4VQANaT56pclPFQEpGIUchB1X5sk3zEP9YDVykD1k3LTjNL0rEgstXCTWow5oT24qAuteR29Pjrh0o4l4wThK5aohYwIyE5iPlA09q5St4uf-b126KHnNl-2XkQCpY_s4mmxBeJqdNJ2kFQi7A8SeByYaOq3GcuBoPLgJr6nn3-Oz7YL4-e9v_y3wkFs5ZWbVcMHDv14zCxVIzIoCYeTv45FGoZfmVX8s8TygXPd3gCEk1u88HYuSE6wbl-e4FCQkaHQ/4q0/vcAkCalWSrKTMnDfeg1OgQ/h2/h001.kxMW6pA7tJhb7Sr3ingJeCEzs9LoFdvubQiG0ujXDoU) [READ THE STORY](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMdUS12fSrk6MMZIR1Ut2K6fzNFGLRHmgujr_IKbsEumaNtgSoUNzi2tORB9F0hjLvnPyr5Itx5Tc3vjSiipEyky-gCEVqAf9WN81VD3QLqKoYnpVYEvSob6VDUZgWC4VQANaT56pclPFQEpGIUchB1X5sk3zEP9YDVykD1k3LTjNL0rEgstXCTWow5oT24qAurU7AherYp3Ghy6e-No_LeLhyozxUV6jgnWmfMEju56gefh2tBPvivtU-9GcESsVUZ5eYmLC4LJ7vvHtH7MhHTIP0wfkqCMqcv4JGYkfWRnRYE_EuCreztKB9xJpSBCUA0UNSbec-SRZFYmPkBYMQ8GqV1WP3EBrfMKuIsBvW9sebdJnMSvAryUmlrjpnUjsiQ/4q0/vcAkCalWSrKTMnDfeg1OgQ/h3/h001.8R89_juDSaflLY5mSZOb_uAQgiH-kUGSD9yPNULjgtU) According to the memos, Justice Alito worried that the MAGA justices’ inability to swoop in and stop the Obama environmental plan would result in a hit to the Supreme Court’s “institutional legitimacy.” A decade later, the Supreme Court is receiving its lowest approval ratings of all time. The American people are losing faith in the justice system and the Court’s work. T**he shadow docket is the perfect example of why. Instead of a Court that makes cautious, considered decisions that they carefully explain to the public, we get rushed, one-paragraph rulings with no explanation.** This is not what democracy is supposed to look like. The uncovered memos expose that Chief Justice Roberts didn’t appear to consider any downsides to his radical shift in Court behavior, and weighed no alternatives. Within a matter of days, one man took it upon himself to build a justice system that put wealthy, powerful extremists above the Constitution. **This is exactly why United for Democracy exists.** We the People need a Supreme Court that will represent us, protect our democracy, and operate transparently. That’s why we’re building the mass movement to fight for court reform now. **[Between the abuse of the shadow docket and the capture of the Supreme Court by MAGA extremists, United for Democracy is working to expose corruption in our justice system. Chip in today to support the fight to bring transparency and legitimacy back to the Supreme Court.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsQNarR6PCR1lUtXpWTyhe62tkxb8fszLuQdDSl49kDqzof65CWxO-APQxcM4hyQNjUyeMpmmBfllhYccuG5FrZxVoEjBKcBKBve0CM4IcudE6guRIdsoWzudvFy8guRzL1gv9BFHgr1OQWcfSC9W5om6pz-qsKRGp8gzEfbsfcNSL2NxCFbe5ItALQZmtRmHxRVNBm-6huvz6S1zAhD7awjGKqcCIGh618U0v_lAq2D58Y7rp92lmFS8T2vu1wWSzOfYCRb44fGoFNi8CxJmxN/4q0/vcAkCalWSrKTMnDfeg1OgQ/h4/h001.EHpFDcpxmymnznMQ0H2hDRmw7UwhaWVu6StHHZBviVM)** Thank you for keeping the spotlight on the Supreme Court, Ken’Travius Coleman

Our public lands are the places we hunt, fish, hike, and pass down to our kids. Our water is the lifeblood of our farms, ranches, and rural communities. And it’s the responsibility we all share to protect both for the next generation.

* * *
Broadcasting live from the floor of the Cincinnati airport -- **yes, really, sitting on the terminal floor at CVG** -- Cliff Schecter and David Shuster sit down with legendary Democratic strategist Joe Trippi for the kind of conversation you can only have when the ground is moving under the whole political map.
* Tucker Carlson is on camera apologizing for "misleading" people into voting for Trump.
* Marjorie Taylor Greene is calling for the 25th Amendment.
* Alex Jones wants Trump removed.
* The Lyft drivers in Ohio are ranting unprompted.

The MAGA coalition isn't cracking -- it's coming apart in public, in real time, and the question is no longer _if_ it collapses but _how far it takes the Republican Party with it._
[ Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=195051243&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk1MDUxMjQzLCJpYXQiOjE3NzY4OTU3NTQsImV4cCI6MTc3OTQ4Nzc1NCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.DcBqhCpbtJGDfxs70esUXBpKuqjty1711_YrKi_pmcw)
Trippi brings the receipts that turn the vibes into a political earthquake. Trump's approval with independents has cratered to 27% -- a number not seen since Nixon was resigning. The "double haters" who normally sit out midterms are voting 58-20 for Democrats, an unprecedented break. Latino support is moving at a scale veteran strategist Mike Madrid calls the largest he's ever measured. Iowa is in play in ways the Beltway hasn't caught up to. So is Ohio, Maine, Alabama -- and even Mississippi is in single digits.
Trippi, who's been running national campaigns since 1979, has a one-sentence verdict: _" I have not seen anything like this in the entire time I've been doing this."_ **What he says next -- about how big the 2026 wave actually gets, how Trump tries to steal it anyway, and which 2028 candidate is already running the right play -- is the reason you need to watch the whole hour.**

clean_body: The biggest National Memorial Day Parade yet | | | Patriot, It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250th birthday. Patriot, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. Patriot, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you. The 2026 National Memorial Day Parade is a once-in-a-lifetime moment where we need to do all we can to honor our country and our veterans. Bigger crowds. More veterans. More young people learning what courage, service, and sacrifice really mean. Historically, AVC has been able to do this at a fraction of what other major public events cost to put on each year. In fact, the entire parade costs about as much as just THREE balloons in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade or TWO floats in the Rose Bowl Parade! That means that every dollar that's contributed by a generous American like you makes a difference for this important event. But I want to reiterate that American Veterans Center does not take ANY federal funding for this event. It is funded entirely by private citizens like you who want to honor those who have sacrificed so much for our country. | | Your support of the American Veterans Center not only helps the parade, but also supports great programs like: Record hundreds of oral histories of veterans from World War II to today before we lose these stories forever. Hold our annual American Veterans Conference, which allows young cadets a chance to hear first-hand from veterans from WWII, Korea, Vietnam, and our modern wars. Produce veteran-focused T.V. documentaries and specials that remind Americans the price of our freedom. But of course, the National Memorial Day Parade is AVC's flagship event honoring America's veterans. And this year's parade will be the largest in their history of hosting the parade. If you've been looking for an opportunity to give back to those who have given so much for our freedom, this is one of the best possible ways you could do it. And for a special group of veterans, this might be one of the last chances we get. You see, with each year that goes by, we lose more and more of our World War II veterans, and for the few we have remaining, traveling to Washington, D.C., for the parade is difficult. | | | | | WWII veterans were a key part of the first parade when it was revived in 2005, as they have been every year since for the last 20 years. But this may be the last year we have the opportunity to have these brave men and women with us for the parade. This year is a rare moment when living witnesses to World War II and America 's 250**th birthday overlap. And no matter how much you can give to this important cause, I want to ask something additional of you. On Memorial Day - not just this momentous year of military milestones, but every year - please join me in honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. Come to the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. Visit a local veterans' cemetery. Send a note to a family of the fallen. Or simply take a quiet moment to think about the men and women who gave their lives to defend OUR country. I believe that while we can never do enough to express our gratitude to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, we can always do a little more. Patriot, thank you for your support of America 's heroes. Sincerely, Gary Sinise Honarary Grand MarshalNational Memorial Day Parade P.S. And for the Greatest Generation in particular, this may be the last time they're able to join us at this year's National Memorial Day Parade. Trump just nominated
another one of his personal lawyers to the bench — and it’s as blatant as
it gets.

Matthew Schwartz, one of Trump’s political puppets, worked to appeal his
conviction in the Manhattan hush money case.

Now Trump wants to hand him a lifetime judgeship, which is a clear
conflict of interest.

Forget qualifications or justice. This is about loyalty alone.

Because when Trump looks at the courts, he doesn’t see an independent
branch of government — he sees a place to stash his allies, protect his
interests, and tilt the system in his favor for decades.

Schwartz joins a growing list of cronies, political operatives, and
loyalists Trump is trying to install across the judiciary whose primary
qualification is that they’ve already gone to bat for Trump.

That’s how you rig a system, and it’s exactly what Trump is doing.

Demand Justice PAC is sounding the alarm and fighting back against this
scheme: mobilizing public pressure, holding senators accountable, and
exposing nominees like Schwartz for what they are.

And that pressure works — but only if we have the resources to keep it up

We have stopped Trump’s attempt to rig the midterms.

Peter — The voters of Virginia just made themselves heard. **We can now unequivocally say that, together, we stopped Donald Trump’s attempt to rig the 2026 midterms through gerrymandering. ** When Trump sparked this crisis by demanding that Texas further gerrymander its congressional map last summer, Republicans greatly underestimated the American people’s capacity to respond and Democrats’ ability to fight back. Republicans moved fast to try to lock in control of Congress through mid-decade redraws. Trump ally Steve Bannon estimated that there were 21 congressional districts Republicans “could pick up now.” _**They were wrong. **_ Instead, voters in California, Indiana, and now Virginia said no. And thanks to the work of the NDRC and our affiliates and partners across the fair maps movement, we fought them to a standstill — taking them to court, rallying voters, and passing responsive maps to ensure this year’s congressional map will be responsive to the will of the people. **Last night’s victory is critical to preserving democracy in the face of relentless attacks — but this fight is far from over. ** Now, all eyes turn to Florida, where Gov. Ron DeSantis is promising to further gerrymander the state, ignoring a ban on mid-decade partisan gerrymandering and protections for minority voters enshrined in the state constitution. We expect to see more attacks on voting rights as Trump and his allies continue to push modern poll taxes and Jim Crow-style voting laws like the SAVE Act. And above all, we are preparing for the Supreme Court’s decision in _Louisiana v. Callais_ , which threatens to tear down the crown jewel of the civil rights movement, the Voting Rights Act, triggering countless new redraws in states across the country. **The Republican attacks on democracy are not over. But last night, we got confirmation that we have the power to stop them.[We must be aggressive every step of the way, and that requires all of us to do our part — make a donation today, and let’s not back down, even for a second.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129979543/616203663/359562654?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_VAResultsWin_email_20260422-NDRC-Tier1-VAResultsWin_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260422-NDRC-Tier1-VAResultsWin_&utm_campaign=VAResultsWin&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjNiYmEzNDcwLTk5M2UtZjExMS04ZWYyLTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=vWo68_vsf3FswBlO8etfWYbUyhaaQyfJb5db7ggtQa4=)** | _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_

clean_body: We have stopped Trump’s attempt to rig the midterms. | Peter — The voters of Virginia just made themselves heard. We can now unequivocally say that, together, we stopped Donald Trump’s attempt to rig the 2026 midterms through gerrymandering. When Trump sparked this crisis by demanding that Texas further gerrymander its congressional map last summer, Republicans greatly underestimated the American people’s capacity to respond and Democrats’ ability to fight back. Republicans moved fast to try to lock in control of Congress through mid-decade redraws. Trump ally Steve Bannon estimated that there were 21 congressional districts Republicans “could pick up now.” They were wrong. Instead, voters in California, Indiana, and now Virginia said no. And thanks to the work of the NDRC and our affiliates and partners across the fair maps movement, we fought them to a standstill — taking them to court, rallying voters, and passing responsive maps to ensure this year’s congressional map will be responsive to the will of the people. Last night’s victory is critical to preserving democracy in the face of relentless attacks — but this fight is far from over. Now, all eyes turn to Florida, where Gov. Ron DeSantis is promising to further gerrymander the state, ignoring a ban on mid-decade partisan gerrymandering and protections for minority voters enshrined in the state constitution. We expect to see more attacks on voting rights as Trump and his allies continue to push modern poll taxes and Jim Crow-style voting laws like the SAVE Act. And above all, we are preparing for the Supreme Court’s decision in Louisiana v. Callais , which threatens to tear down the crown jewel of the civil rights movement, the Voting Rights Act, triggering countless new redraws in states across the country. The Republican attacks on democracy are not over. subject: What I told the POLITICO Health Care Summit
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
An overwhelming number of voters support a plan like Medicare For All.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260422-6163-footer&t=1&akid=6163%2E420207%2EELMehR)
Peter,
At yesterday’s POLITICO Health Care Summit, I made one thing clear:
**Voters across the country — including in swing districts — are ready for Medicare For All.**
[](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260422.Uejoch&refcode=em20260422-6163&t=2&akid=6163%2E420207%2EELMehR)
Right now health care is the number one cost concern for Americans. In an economy where working people are struggling to survive, you _cannot_ be too left on health care.
**The situation that we have now is so unacceptable that people aren’t looking for incremental changes — they want us to go big.**
That’s why an overwhelming number of voters support a plan like Medicare For All, where the government provides your insurance card from birth to death with comprehensive care. That includes 90% of Democrats, 60% of independents, and even 20% of Republicans.
This will be a defining issue in the midterms, and we need to keep building momentum for _truly_ universal health care. I’m working every day both inside and outside of Congress to do just that, but I need your support.
I don’t have billionaires and health insurance CEOs funding my campaign. Everything I do is powered by grassroots donations from people like you.
[**Peter, can I count on you to help me keep building the momentum for Medicare For All with a donation of $3 today?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260422.Uejoch&refcode=em20260422-6163&amount=3&t=3&akid=6163%2E420207%2EELMehR)

Together, we can make universal health care a reality. But it’s going to take all of us doing our part.
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

name: AOC
subject: Redistricting in Virginia
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
We have asked Republicans for 10 years to ban partisan gerrymandering. And for 10 years, Republicans have said no.
Republicans have fought for partisan gerrymanders across the United States of America. These are the rules that _they_ have set.
The Republican Party wanted to start this. They did this in North Carolina. They drew out three Democratic members of Congress in North Carolina. They did it in Texas.
What they’re mad at is that they have been accustomed to a Democratic Party that rolls over, doesn’t fight, and takes everything sitting down. And what they’re mad at right now is that **we are here in a new day**.
We have been asking the Democratic Party to stand up and fight, and now they did — and now the Republican Party doesn’t like the fact that they are fighting against someone who actually will stand up for the American people.
So if Republicans decide that they would like to revisit a ban on partisan gerrymandering, I welcome them. We have the bill right here to end this all today.
But they don’t want to, because **they like pursuing and continuing to enact an unfair electoral landscape**.
So we have an obligation to defend ourselves.
More soon,
Alexandria
The midterms are coming, and we must be ready to defend the working class against the rise of authoritarianism in this country.

Friends, at a moment when families everywhere are stretching their dollars and wondering when the affordability crisis will end, Amazon has been working behind the scenes to make your life more expensive.
What Amazon is doing is called price fixing — a practice that’s not only unethical and unfair for consumers, but illegal.
We’re fighting to put a stop to Amazon’s illegal price fixing and collusion by taking them to court, and now we’re making the evidence in the case public so Americans can see exactly what’s happening behind closed doors.
So let’s name names. Target, Walmart, Chewy, Best Buy, Home Depot, Wayfair, and others – these are some of the competing retailers and vendors that Amazon has been colluding with to raise prices across the market. As a result, consumers have nowhere else to turn to for lower prices, and Amazon continues to rake in profits.
It all starts with Amazon demanding that vendors “fix,” “correct,” “increase,” “raise,” or “look into” the prices of their products on other retailers’ websites. If they don’t comply, then Amazon threatens to pull their products, restrict their advertising, or demand financial compensation.
Levi's and Walmart agreed to raise the price of khaki pants. Allergan and Walmart raised the price of eye drops. Hanes and Target raised the price of apparel. And pet treat vendors jacked up prices on Chewy. The list goes on, spanning years and product lines.
The result is that you pay more on everything, no matter where you purchase it.
Price fixing is illegal, and that’s why we're taking them to court.
In February, I filed for a preliminary injunction to halt Amazon's illegal conduct while our lawsuit proceeds. The injunction hearing is set for July, and this case goes to trial in January 2027.
The Trump administration won't lift a finger to hold Amazon accountable or tackle our affordability crisis. But I will — and I am.
If you’re with me, will you help power our work with a contribution right now? Anything you can give before the end of April will have a meaningful impact on fights just like this one. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26?amount=50]

name: Jon Ossoff
subject: Saturday's rally in Augusta
disclaimer_text: paid for by ending utility assistance for families, canceling affordable housing programs, and cutting cancer research
body:
# [](https://act.electjon.com/go/4629?t=1&akid=2153%2E5691347%2E_nfMLS)

On Saturday, I rallied a crowd in Augusta to oppose this Administration’s unprecedented attack on our Constitution and the rule of law.
[](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-april26.1MDdBw&refcode=em260422-2-f&t=2&akid=2153%2E5691347%2E_nfMLS)
[(You can watch my speech here on YouTube.)](https://act.electjon.com/go/4741?t=3&akid=2153%2E5691347%2E_nfMLS)
Here's what I said:
Hello, Augusta!
Augusta, are you ready to work? Are you ready to win? Who came here today because you love our country? Who came here today because you're just a little bit mad? I feel you.
It is so great to be with you here in Augusta, home of Fort Gordon.
_Now Augusta, I don't know if you saw, but JD Vance was in Georgia this week.**Don't worry, no one showed up.** The stadium was empty. Did you see that? But JD came to UGA to attack the Pope two days after Donald Trump depicted himself as Jesus Christ._
The faithless President depicts himself as Christ while he plunges the nation into wars of choice, while he and his family rake in billions from foreign princes, while he plunders our health care to cut taxes for the rich.
Meanwhile, rent, power, groceries, and health care have all hit all-time highs this year. Ground beef's up 20% since Trump took office. Coffee, 40%.
Health premiums through the roof, and remember, while you pay more for everything, the First Family's wealth is growing by billions of dollars. Because they're crooks, and everybody knows it.
We were promised a Golden Age. Instead, the economy's lost 75,000 manufacturing jobs just since Trump launched his big illegal tariffs.
Hiring's at its lowest rate since 2020. Zero net private sector job creation for the past six months.
Here in Georgia, International Paper closed its plants in Savannah and Riceboro, more than 1,000 jobs gone. SK just laid off almost 1,000 workers at their EV battery plant over in Commerce because of this administration's war on renewable energy.
Now we were told MAGA was for the working class. Do you remember that? **But this is a government of, by, and for the ultra rich.**
They are the elites they pretend to hate. That's why they gutted Medicaid and let health insurance premiums double for more than 20 million Americans to fund another tax cut for the rich.
And did you hear what this man said two weeks ago? "It's not possible," the President said, "for us to take care of daycare, Medicaid, or Medicare."
He said we can only afford to fund war, then released a budget demanding $1.5 trillion for the Pentagon next year alone, paid for by ending utility assistance for families, canceling affordable housing programs, and cutting cancer research. All to fund a huge increase for the military industrial complex.
**Because draft-dodging Donald loves sending other people's children to war.**
Just two weeks into this war, the White House told us they'd need $200 billion to fund it.
_Let me just put that in perspective for you. $200 billion would fund a decade — 10 full years — of nationwide, universal pre-kindergarten. Instead, a war no one voted for and no one can explain._
And the daily, the hourly, lying to the American public about why we're at war, whether we've won, what's been agreed to. Not to mention the insane genocidal threats.
Let's review the record:
On day 10 of the war, the President said, "The war is very complete." That was day 10.
Then day 11, "Going to be finished pretty quickly."
Day 12, "We won."
Day 21, "Getting very close."
Day 32, "Leaving very soon."
Day 40, "Total and complete victory."
Yesterday, day 49, Trump said Iran had opened the Strait. Except this morning, the Strait was closed, and it looks like Iran hit a cargo ship.
Here's what we know. Thirteen brave Americans killed and hundreds wounded. Thousands of civilians dead. Military equipment it will take years to replace. Skyrocketing inflation. Massive damage to our reputation and position in the world.
Meanwhile, Iran's ballistic missiles and drones are not destroyed. We replaced Ayatollah Khamenei with Ayatollah Khamenei.
The regime is intact, along with its ability to throttle the global energy supply, along with its stockpile of highly enriched uranium, which it only assembled after Donald Trump shredded President Obama's Iran deal. Do you remember that?
See, the Obama administration had done actual work led by actual diplomats. Trump literally sends his golf buddy Steve and his son-in-law Jared.
How much do you guys know about Jared Kushner, Ivanka's husband? He's on the Saudi payroll for $2 billion dollars. Did you know that?
And now he's leading American diplomacy in the Middle East, apparently while at the very same time asking princes and sheikhs across the Arab world to give him billions more.
Don't take my word for it. Look it up for yourself.
Can you imagine, like a normal sitting U.S. ambassador just hitting up Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for billions of dollars? But he's a Trump, a royal, a princeling. _The rules are for us, not for them._
And it's not just Jared getting in on the action. A company owned in part by Eric and Don Jr. has been pitching Gulf kingdoms on its drone interceptors during this war.
The Financial Times reported, "Pete Hegseth's broker looked to buy defense fund before Iran attack." _I tell you what, never before have we seen so little effort to hide so much corruption._
**The Mar-a-Lago mafia has taken American corruption to spectacular new heights, but corruption in America runs a lot deeper than Donald Trump.** Because how does American politics really work?
It's coin-operated. Money goes in, favors come out. It's been running on secret money, corporate money, billionaire money. Both sides. _Citizens United_ was the worst court decision in modern American history.
It's why members of Congress don't listen to the people; they listen to their donors. And this corruption is why insurance companies get away with denying your claim for a procedure you needed to save your life.
This corruption is why Big Tech's still allowed to spy on us and track our every move and sell our private lives to the highest bidder. This corruption is why the ultra rich get tax cuts while you pay more for everything.
And beneath it all, a lazy, cynical expedience in Congress and in both political parties, serving donors and reciting poll-tested talking points with no higher purpose than winning the next election.
A politics unmoored from fixed moral principles and incapable of inspiration or great national achievement. **And all of this gave rise to a depraved President who exploits this rot to empower and enrich himself.**
_But Augusta, it doesn't have to be this way._
Everywhere I go across our state, no matter their political party, people are telling me they're desperate for change and for new ideas. The young couple expecting their first child who wonder how they'll afford a crib and a stroller, let alone a first home, and their health insurance just went up $1,000 a month.
The student working through college who still needs food stamps to make rent, whose conscience can't stand their tax dollars being used to lock up immigrant children at home or to kill innocent children overseas.
The South Georgia farmer whose costs rise and earnings fall each year, whose kids have left the family farm, who had to wait almost two years for federal aid after the hurricane. See, they want us to solve problems, and it's no mystery what problems need solving.
Right at the top of our list here in Georgia is our state's health care emergency. And it's an emergency that some of our so-called leaders try to dress up as normal.
They try to numb us to the suffering they've caused. They've continued to block Medicaid expansion, while Georgia's lost 21 hospitals in 20 years.
Last year, they gutted Medicaid nationally, and already one labor and delivery unit in Georgia has closed, citing those Medicaid cuts, with more pain coming for hospitals and clinics and nursing homes.
And then, the Affordable Care Act cuts, which caused nearly a quarter of a million Georgians to lose insurance in the first three months of this year.
All this, when here in Georgia we already have the second highest uninsured rate in the nation, the third fewest mental health providers, the fourth worst newborn weight at birth.
Just wrap your head around this: When you're born in the state of Georgia, your life expectancy is shorter than if you'd been born in Lebanon, a country that's been in a state of intermittent war for decades.
And now consider that our state's economy, just our state, is 40 times larger than Lebanon's national economy, but they're living longer than us.
The legendary civil rights leader Marian Wright Edelman said, "We don't have a money problem. We have a profound values and priorities problem." Because this isn't just the way it is or the way it has to be.
All this needless death and suffering and misery is a choice. Georgia's leaders have chosen to leave Georgians without health insurance and without hospitals. So let's stop pretending those responsible are competent, serious people.
They're over in Atlanta, having a steak at The Palm, handing out your tax dollars to their donors, while women hemorrhage in Georgia labor wards because they didn't get prenatal care.
And then the insurance companies that fill their campaign coffers are allowed to deny and delay the health care Georgians need.
The Monroe County mother of three with cancer, denied a liver transplant, who had to fight her insurance company while being told she had just six months to live.
The retired Georgia teacher who'd paid $100,000 into a cancer policy, only to be diagnosed with cancer and then have her claims denied.
_True stories. And just the tip of the iceberg._
The thousands of Georgia children denied health care by insurance companies, many of them foster children, while in the last few years, the State of Georgia threw tens of thousands of kids off health insurance altogether.
No child in Georgia should be turned away from the doctor because they don't have health insurance. No child in Georgia should have to go without a checkup or be denied the hearing or dental or vision or mental health care they need to be happy and healthy and to thrive.
How can we say we're doing right when children are being turned away from the doctor, when insurance companies deny Georgia kids and Georgia families care they need, when state officials turn a blind eye to the abuse and mistreatment of Georgia's foster kids, some of whom are literally trafficked while in the care of the State?
All of this, the corruption, the callous neglect, and needless suffering signal not just a political crisis, but a moral one.
I look at the agenda in Washington today, advanced by so many who drape themselves in the banner of righteous faith, and I ask, where in scripture are we commanded to deny care to the sick?
To take from those with the least and give to those with the most? To hunt down the refugee and take her from her infant child?
**But our task is not just to contain this wickedness, it's to repair the brokenness underneath it.**
Today's small and self-serving politics has distanced us from the great national spirit that defeated fascism, that landed men on the moon, that passed civil rights laws.
And yet last week, while our President flailed in the Strait, the American spacecraft Artemis, with four heroes on board, returned humanity to the far side of the moon, recalling the best of American genius and strength and achievement and sending back images that remind us not to take for granted our precious, fragile planet.
The United States is still destined for greatness, but only united will we meet the challenges and seize the opportunities of our time: to guarantee great health care for every American, to unleash an affordable housing boom and save our family farms, to harness new technologies for the good of the many, and not the few, to make America the world leader on human rights and return nations to the path of peaceful coexistence.
**But none of this is possible without victory this November.**
"One if by land, two if by sea." Do y'all remember that? 251 years ago today, late on April 18th, 1775, two lanterns hung in the steeple of the Old North Church in Boston, Massachusetts, the sign for Paul Revere to ride.
At dawn the next day in Lexington and Concord, the minutemen fought and won their first battle against the Crown. See, our nation is founded on a rejection of kingdom and on the radical idea that all human beings have a natural right to liberty.
Dr. King said of our Declaration of Independence, "Never before in the history of the world has a sociopolitical document expressed in such profound, eloquent, and unequivocal language the dignity and worth of human personality."
And from those founding ideals, despite our sins and through courageous struggle, the flame of American freedom has grown brighter and bolder and given hope to the whole world.
But today we face a President who's embarked on this unmistakable project, not to lead us, but to rule us as subjects. He deifies and enriches himself, as he adorns the White House in gold and raises a massive force of masked federal police.
The President who once tried to overturn his own defeat now tries to jail elected leaders of the opposition, prosecute Americans who defy or criticize him, and seize control of elections nationwide.
As he indulges in careless militarism around the world, he plans a monument to himself so tall it will disrupt air traffic into our nation's capital.
For all this, the founders of our Republic must be turning in their graves, but they gave us the tools to fix it, freedoms guaranteed at our founding, made real through struggle and sacrifice in places like Seneca Falls and Selma and Stonewall.
And of all the freedoms at stake, none is more powerful or precious than the right to vote.
In Georgia, we know better than anyone that the election deniers are on the march. The Fulton County raid, the executive order attacking voting, the MAGA loyalists on our state election board, they've made their plans very clear.
_But Georgians are prepared to answer with a mobilization so massive and with a defense of voting rights so fierce that no plot against the franchise can foil the will of the people._
Because how foolish of them to come to the cradle of the civil rights movement to spread those lies and seize our ballots.
How foolish to launch an attack on voting rights here in Georgia, at the political and spiritual center of the very Black history they seek to erase.
_Augusta, their attacks only strengthen our resolve, and if all of us here do what we must do, the sound of feet marching to the polls this fall will be heard in every corner of our state and all the way on high, where Congressman Lewis will look down and see a job well done. Augusta, are you ready to win?_
A wave is building, the kind that comes once a generation, when people have been pushed too far and they decide all at once and all together that enough is enough.
Across Georgia, more and more of every background and belief reject this chaos and corruption.
It's not just Democrats and Independents. Republicans pull me aside, or they call me on the phone, and they tell me they're voting for a Democrat for the first time in their lives. And we welcome them.
Five years ago, in the early hours of January 6th, 2021, right before the President's mob sacked the Capitol, hope broke out across the nation because the people of Georgia had spoken so clearly. Because Georgia sent the young Jewish son of an immigrant and a Black pastor who holds Dr. King's pulpit at Ebenezer Baptist Church to the U.S. Senate.
We did it before. We'll do it again. And as long as we don't give in to doubt or despair or division, our victories will be so decisive that no half-baked plot hatched in the White House will foil the will of the people.
Because history is calling the question: What kind of people are we? And Georgia is ready to answer once again that the measure of our success is not how many of the poorest and most vulnerable families we hunt down and shackle and imprison and deport.
The measure of our success is whether each generation achieves greater health and prosperity than the last and whether we live up to the promise of equal justice for all. Georgia is ready to send a message that we will bow to no king.
**So Augusta, are you ready to work? Are you ready to win? Let's get it done.**
Thank you so much, Augusta.
👋 Wait! Before you go... 👋
Jon Ossoff in Georgia is the ONLY Democratic Senator running for reelection in a state Trump won.
He is MAGA's #1 target in the 2026 midterms.
**[If you can afford it, please rush $5 to Jon's reelection campaign today.](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-april26.1MDdBw&refcode=em260422-2-f&t=4&akid=2153%2E5691347%2E_nfMLS)**
**[DONATE NOW](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-april26.1MDdBw&refcode=em260422-2-f&t=5&akid=2153%2E5691347%2E_nfMLS)**

Paid for by Jon Ossoff for Senate
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Thank you for supporting Jon Ossoff. Email is a critical way to keep up with Jon and his work in the US Senate, but you can click [here](https://act.electjon.com/signup/fewer-emails-signup/?t=6&akid=2153%2E5691347%2E_nfMLS) to sign up to receive fewer emails, or click [here](https://act.electjon.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=7&akid=2153%2E5691347%2E_nfMLS) if you'd like to unsubscribe.

A politics unmoored from fixed moral principles and incapable of inspiration or great national achievement. And all of this gave rise to a depraved President who exploits this rot to empower and enrich himself. But Augusta, it doesn't have to be this way. Everywhere I go across our state, no matter their political party, people are telling me they're desperate for change and for new ideas. The young couple expecting their first child who wonder how they'll afford a crib and a stroller, let alone a first home, and their health insurance just went up $1,000 a month. The student working through college who still needs food stamps to make rent, whose conscience can't stand their tax dollars being used to lock up immigrant children at home or to kill innocent children overseas. The South Georgia farmer whose costs rise and earnings fall each year, whose kids have left the family farm, who had to wait almost two years for federal aid after the hurricane. See, they want us to solve problems, and it's no mystery what problems need solving. Right at the top of our list here in Georgia is our state's health care emergency. And it's an emergency that some of our so-called leaders try to dress up as normal. They try to numb us to the suffering they've caused. They've continued to block Medicaid expansion, while Georgia's lost 21 hospitals in 20 years. Last year, they gutted Medicaid nationally, and already one labor and delivery unit in Georgia has closed, citing those Medicaid cuts, with more pain coming for hospitals and clinics and nursing homes. And then, the Affordable Care Act cuts, which caused nearly a quarter of a million Georgians to lose insurance in the first three months of this year. All this, when here in Georgia we already have the second highest uninsured rate in the nation, the third fewest mental health providers, the fourth worst newborn weight at birth. Just wrap your head around this: When you're born in the state of Georgia, your life expectancy is shorter than if you'd been born in Lebanon, a country that's been in a state of intermittent war for decades. And now consider that our state's economy, just our state, is 40 times larger than Lebanon's national economy, but they're living longer than us. The legendary civil rights leader Marian Wright Edelman said, "We don't have a money problem. We have a profound values and priorities problem." Because this isn't just the way it is or the way it has to be. All this needless death and suffering and misery is a choice. Georgia's leaders have chosen to leave Georgians without health insurance and without hospitals. So let's stop pretending those responsible are competent, serious people. They're over in Atlanta, having a steak at The Palm, handing out your tax dollars to their donors, while women hemorrhage in Georgia labor wards because they didn't get prenatal care. And then the insurance companies that fill their campaign coffers are allowed to deny and delay the health care Georgians need. The Monroe County mother of three with cancer, denied a liver transplant, who had to fight her insurance company while being told she had just six months to live. The retired Georgia teacher who'd paid $100,000 into a cancer policy, only to be diagnosed with cancer and then have her claims denied. True stories. And just the tip of the iceberg. The thousands of Georgia children denied health care by insurance companies, many of them foster children, while in the last few years, the State of Georgia threw tens of thousands of kids off health insurance altogether. No child in Georgia should be turned away from the doctor because they don't have health insurance. No child in Georgia should have to go without a checkup or be denied the hearing or dental or vision or mental health care they need to be happy and healthy and to thrive. How can we say we're doing right when children are being turned away from the doctor, when insurance companies deny Georgia kids and Georgia families care they need, when state officials turn a blind eye to the abuse and mistreatment of Georgia's foster kids, some of whom are literally trafficked while in the care of the State? All of this, the corruption, the callous neglect, and needless suffering signal not just a political crisis, but a moral one. I look at the agenda in Washington today, advanced by so many who drape themselves in the banner of righteous faith, and I ask, where in scripture are we commanded to deny care to the sick? To take from those with the least and give to those with the most? To hunt down the refugee and take her from her infant child? But our task is not just to contain this wickedness, it's to repair the brokenness underneath it. Today's small and self-serving politics has distanced us from the great national spirit that defeated fascism, that landed men on the moon, that passed civil rights laws. And yet last week, while our President flailed in the Strait, the American spacecraft Artemis, with four heroes on board, returned humanity to the far side of the moon, recalling the best of American genius and strength and achievement and sending back images that remind us not to take for granted our precious, fragile planet. The United States is still destined for greatness, but only united will we meet the challenges and seize the opportunities of our time: to guarantee great health care for every American, to unleash an affordable housing boom and save our family farms, to harness new technologies for the good of the many, and not the few, to make America the world leader on human rights and return nations to the path of peaceful coexistence. But none of this is possible without victory this November. "One if by land, two if by sea." Do y'all remember that? 251 years ago today, late on April 18th, 1775, two lanterns hung in the steeple of the Old North Church in Boston, Massachusetts, the sign for Paul Revere to ride. At dawn the next day in Lexington and Concord, the minutemen fought and won their first battle against the Crown. See, our nation is founded on a rejection of kingdom and on the radical idea that all human beings have a natural right to liberty. Dr. King said of our Declaration of Independence, "Never before in the history of the world has a sociopolitical document expressed in such profound, eloquent, and unequivocal language the dignity and worth of human personality." And from those founding ideals, despite our sins and through courageous struggle, the flame of American freedom has grown brighter and bolder and given hope to the whole world. But today we face a President who's embarked on this unmistakable project, not to lead us, but to rule us as subjects. He deifies and enriches himself, as he adorns the White House in gold and raises a massive force of masked federal police. The President who once tried to overturn his own defeat now tries to jail elected leaders of the opposition, prosecute Americans who defy or criticize him, and seize control of elections nationwide. As he indulges in careless militarism around the world, he plans a monument to himself so tall it will disrupt air traffic into our nation's capital. For all this, the founders of our Republic must be turning in their graves, but they gave us the tools to fix it, freedoms guaranteed at our founding, made real through struggle and sacrifice in places like Seneca Falls and Selma and Stonewall. And of all the freedoms at stake, none is more powerful or precious than the right to vote. In Georgia, we know better than anyone that the election deniers are on the march. The Fulton County raid, the executive order attacking voting, the MAGA loyalists on our state election board, they've made their plans very clear. But Georgians are prepared to answer with a mobilization so massive and with a defense of voting rights so fierce that no plot against the franchise can foil the will of the people. Because how foolish of them to come to the cradle of the civil rights movement to spread those lies and seize our ballots. How foolish to launch an attack on voting rights here in Georgia, at the political and spiritual center of the very Black history they seek to erase. Augusta, their attacks only strengthen our resolve, and if all of us here do what we must do, the sound of feet marching to the polls this fall will be heard in every corner of our state and all the way on high, where Congressman Lewis will look down and see a job well done. Augusta, are you ready to win? A wave is building, the kind that comes once a generation, when people have been pushed too far and they decide all at once and all together that enough is enough. Across Georgia, more and more of every background and belief reject this chaos and corruption. It's not just Democrats and Independents. Republicans pull me aside, or they call me on the phone, and they tell me they're voting for a Democrat for the first time in their lives. And we welcome them. Five years ago, in the early hours of January 6th, 2021, right before the President's mob sacked the Capitol, hope broke out across the nation because the people of Georgia had spoken so clearly. Because Georgia sent the young Jewish son of an immigrant and a Black pastor who holds Dr. King's pulpit at Ebenezer Baptist Church to the U.S. Senate. We did it before. We'll do it again. And as long as we don't give in to doubt or despair or division, our victories will be so decisive that no half-baked plot hatched in the White House will foil the will of the people. Because history is calling the question: What kind of people are we? And Georgia is ready to answer once again that the measure of our success is not how many of the poorest and most vulnerable families we hunt down and shackle and imprison and deport. The measure of our success is whether each generation achieves greater health and prosperity than the last and whether we live up to the promise of equal justice for all. Georgia is ready to send a message that we will bow to no king. So Augusta, are you ready to work? Are you ready to win? Let's get it done. Thank you so much, Augusta. 👋 Wait! Before you go... 👋 Jon Ossoff in Georgia is the ONLY Democratic Senator running for reelection in a state Trump won. He is MAGA's #1 target in the 2026 midterms. Paid for by Jon Ossoff for Senate

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: RFK Jr’s hearing
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
The “discount” is actually a price hike.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2868%2E4032634%2EGFQWRK)
---
Congress questioned HHS Secretary Kennedy this week on a whole bunch of issues: Vaccine misinformation, health care cuts, and cancer research cuts. I had the chance to ask RFK Jr. about TrumpRx and these “massive” deals for patients that he’s been boasting about. Right after Trump and the Republicans cut health care for millions of families, the president launched his TrumpRx website as the answer for Americans who were worried about health care costs. The website invites patients to “find the world's lowest prices on prescription drugs.” He claimed that TrumpRx has reduced drug prices by as much as _600%._ **600%.** In that instance, drug companies would be paying us to take their drugs, which doesn’t make any sense. Health Secretary Kennedy explained that President Trump has a “different way of calculating percentages” and that there’s “two ways” of calculating percentages — saying “if you have a $600 drug and you reduce it to $10, that's a 600% reduction.” What! So we’re just re-inventing math now? In his own example, that would be a 98.33% reduction. But 600% sounds a whole lot flashier than 98.33% — if that’s even true. But there’s another layer to this: TrumpRx is actually steering patients to buy more expensive brand-name drugs to pad the profits of Big Pharma companies. Let’s do some real math here: There’s a heartburn medication called Protonix that is currently sold for $200 on TrumpRx. But a generic version of the same drug sold at Costco is just $16. In the real world, $200 is a heck of a lot more expensive than $16. But TrumpRx is not promoting the cheaper option — just the more expensive brand-name drug. Promoting brand-name drugs over cheaper generic options of the same exact drug is a tried-and-true Big Pharma tactic to get people to buy more expensive drugs. The so-called “discount” is actually a price hike. Too often, the TrumpRx website is nothing more than another Trump scam — just like Trump University and Trump Steaks, and just about everything else associated with his name. This time they’re targeting and tricking sick Americans with fake drug “discounts” that actually help Big Pharma’s bottom line — and I’m not standing for it. If they cared at all about taking on Big Pharma, they wouldn’t use these shady tactics to lie about drug “savings” on TrumpRx. If they cared at all about making health care more affordable, they wouldn't have kicked millions of Americans off their health insurance. **I’m going to keep exposing the truth, forcing transparency and oversight, and fighting to lower health care costs for patients.** Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth

# **Trump announces Iran will spare 8 women from execution after his personal plea**
President Donald Trump **[announced Wednesday](https://substack.com/redirect/9e0eb740-a9c9-4664-aa99-3b976c5d86b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that Iran will no longer execute eight women after he pleaded Tuesday for their freedom, writing on Truth Social "I have just been informed that the eight women protestors who were going to be executed tonight in Iran will no longer be killed. Four will be released immediately, and four will be sentenced to one month in prison." Trump said "I very much appreciate that Iran, and its leaders, respected my request, as President of the United States, and terminated the planned execution."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9e0eb740-a9c9-4664-aa99-3b976c5d86b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Iran denies execution plans, claims Trump "misled by fake news"**: Iran's judiciary denied the eight women were ever set for execution, claiming "Trump was misled once again by fake news" and that "some of them have been released, while others face charges that, if convictions are upheld, would at most result in imprisonment." However, human rights groups contest this--one woman, Bita Hemmati, was sentenced to death for allegedly throwing objects at Iranian forces during January protests, and two others (Golnaz Naraghi, 37, and Venus Hosseininejad, 28) have been out on bail since late March.
* **Context of US-Iran negotiations** : The announcement came as Trump extended a two-week cease-fire with Iran while US negotiators await Tehran's reply to the latest American offer to end the nearly two-month conflict.

subject: Keeping CA-32’s priorities front and center
body:
Keeping focus on what's important

| | | | | [|
---](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=15bd062587&e=53c7d12fc7)
| | | | | | Dear Peter,I’ve been spending time across CA-32 listening to residents, small business owners, and community leaders. A consistent set of priorities is clear wherever I go:– The rising cost of living and what it will actually take to make it more manageable
– Homelessness spending and whether it is producing measurable, visible results
– Abolishing ICE and creating humane pathways for immigration, not militarized protocols
– Federal dollars that require stronger accountability and clearer outcomes
– Public safety and day-to-day community stabilityThese are the issues that shape daily life in the district.A recent Los Angeles Times analysis of political messaging made a broader point that reflects what I’m hearing locally: voters are more focused on whether leaders are clearly addressing tangible problems in their communities.That’s exactly what people in CA-32 are asking for: more clarity on what is being done to address local challenges and how success is measured.That’s the approach I’m taking.I’m continuing to raise these issues directly, asking more specific questions about what is working and what is not, and keeping attention focused on solutions and outcomes. After 31 years of representation by Brad Sherman, many residents feel these priorities have not received attention or follow-through. In fact many residents feel they have been abandoned and ignored by Brad Sherman. My goal is simple: keep these local issues at the center of the conversation and push for clearer accountability on results. And as always, keep the feedback from the community front and center in a 2-way conversation. [**If that’s the kind of approach you support, I’d be grateful to have you involved.**](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=07853aca17&e=53c7d12fc7)

clean_body: Keeping focus on what's important | | | | | | | | | | | Dear Peter,I’ve been spending time across CA-32 listening to residents, small business owners, and community leaders. A consistent set of priorities is clear wherever I go:– The rising cost of living and what it will actually take to make it more manageable – Homelessness spending and whether it is producing measurable, visible results – Abolishing ICE and creating humane pathways for immigration, not militarized protocols – Federal dollars that require stronger accountability and clearer outcomes – Public safety and day-to-day community stabilityThese are the issues that shape daily life in the district.A recent Los Angeles Times analysis of political messaging made a broader point that reflects what I’m hearing locally: voters are more focused on whether leaders are clearly addressing tangible problems in their communities.That’s exactly what people in CA-32 are asking for: more clarity on what is being done to address local challenges and how success is measured.That’s the approach I’m taking.I’m continuing to raise these issues directly, asking more specific questions about what is working and what is not, and keeping attention focused on solutions and outcomes. After 31 years of representation by Brad Sherman, many residents feel these priorities have not received attention or follow-through. In fact many residents feel they have been abandoned and ignored by Brad Sherman. My goal is simple: keep these local issues at the center of the conversation and push for clearer accountability on results. And as always, keep the feedback from the community front and center in a 2-way conversation. | | AhujaDemocratic Candidate for Congress (CA-32) | | | | | | mailto: | | | | | | | | | | | Copyright (C) 2026 Christopher Ahuja for Congress. | | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

Content warning: This message references violence and death.

Peter,

Trump and his MAGA allies keep telling us ICE is about safety — that
unleashing them into neighborhoods, homes, and people’s lives is meant to
protect us.

But under his administration, what we’re seeing isn’t safety. It’s fear.

That fear defines daily life for entire communities, as expanded ICE
efforts and lack of accountability leave people constantly wondering who
will be targeted next.

The consequences have been devastating. Since October, at least 29
individuals have died in ICE custody — the highest number on record. Over
6,200 detainees are children. Inside these facilities, people are denied
critical medical care, subjected to abuse, and forced to endure inhumane
living conditions.

And the violence doesn’t stop within those walls — it follows people into
their homes and on the street. Renee Good. Alex Pretti. Keith Porter. Dr.
Linda Davis. Lives taken during encounters with ICE agents who continue to
act without consequence.

This is the reality behind the rhetoric: a system that operates with
force, impunity, and with overwhelming human cost.

We can’t accept that. We can’t allow fear to be rebranded as safety, or
violence to be excused as policy. And we can’t fix a system built on
harming others.

It’s time to abolish ICE.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/signup/20260422-abolish-ice/?source=em20260422-2188&t=1002&akid=2188%2E342411%2EtlOATe ]Sign our petition today to join people standing against this abuse of
power and demand real accountability.

The Squad Victory Fund

Iran Seizes Ships in Hormuz

Iran's Revolutionary Guards seized two container ships in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, hours after President Trump [extended the ceasefire](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLGO4yAURb_G7ojwgwVcUGyTLttuaT3DI3kKxhaQsTRfP0o-YcqrK13dc_7flhty5nL_hxv52tMS97hkSv3kcm9HDlwih04x0tbqAhKMkFoALCUvMEYfQ8QpjOQna80spZrl-PCGJvijrcY1OaW1mgyiCymZWWmJ4Eb27ympAUCBAXeZEWenAqGL1kxrGrTETLVfKh2vNXPA0rE9014DXcK-jdk_ej_aoP4OcB3gikehs72rd6idQ6YBrq8muGIRJ1bx2Ov2-hbcKlIWBz65dSwiEDZKXEngUTkLAPHhBGNByWSTglUr4wC009rOalJOy2TH6uNxcs7cjB20vG_I-fOt_0Lll4efAAAA__8UUoB3) indefinitely, citing a "seriously fractured" Iranian government awaiting Tehran's peace proposal. It marks the Islamic Republic's first seizures since the U.S.-Israel conflict began in February. Iran's foreign minister declared the U.S. naval blockade an ["act of war"](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL1upTAQRp_GdEZmYPkpXGxDd7fdEs31jLmjGINsE5K3j0iTPu33SUdH5_9jeaAEies_3Nim4hfaaQnsyyVxzUdwEklcYSLeclrAQK9NpwGWGBaoyJIjbFzFthmGfjKmnUz1sm3XDn-om1qPhgczNjz2xvsRBgbG0VRib5TpAKCFHsZ6QpzG1jGONPTN06vOYOBU6sTH-QziMBbMb35Pjmu3b1Wwr1KOrNq_CmYF83VddeKzcMr3fy97CqRgxiyoD3TixSmYz6wvCUFLJPYSpXD41PxROJJ2jJm9JNZndIExafFaEkaNa2LO-ieAgrlKlo6bJbkfVGfWDSV8y5VftHy38BUAAP__NbGEfw) in response to the continuing blockade. The White House held its ground, with a spokeswoman saying Trump does not view the seizures as a ceasefire violation because the vessels were not American flagged. Shipping traffic through the strait has largely ground to a halt, with just three vessels transiting the waterway in the past 24 hours, according to [tracking data](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LGOpDAQBNCvMZmRaQOGwMElZHPphainbQ_WGIPsnkPar1-xn7BZSSW9kurfY31gTDG__uLubeGwusOtyQe-Yn7VM1HMLhJ75_xeywoKRql6CbDmtELjrCOHHTXedsaMs1J6Vs1mh0mbCU3oJqNVr_xAZoagdUdODUBDE-1NqR4ANIwwtTPiPGnyODkzds8geoXJF26LPz_PFAkzY32Ho5Bv6dibZDfmswr9R8AiYLmuq6X8pLsUsNy8gEX1dwYBS-WCkeUR5HaU_fMl6xbPKpEZ6e2djAWzvLC0G--pKdadV0wp1tGIXr12jOlnln_x0n8L3wEAAP__5_J1pg). Oil prices rose on the news, with markets watching whether the move signals a breakdown in negotiations before they have formally begun. ★★★
SPLC Indicted on Fraud Charges

A federal grand jury in Montgomery, Alabama, [indicted the Southern Poverty Law Center](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LHO3CAQBOCnsTufYO0fTEGR5ro_bUprYZe7VTC2gLtT3j5yHiHlaKTRp_n1vX2jZCmPn7izrz1tdNCWOfWPlEc7c5RCEjsT8d7qBgrMpJYJYCt5g5E8RUIdR_baWuOUmp0an_4rLHq15LQzznyx1omc1s7Sas2sAo_irym1AMAMBtabQ3TrHBlXskaHNCwKM9d-q3y-QpaIpWP7nY4a-RaPfcz-2fvZhvnHAPcB7ngW_rSrukLtEjMPcG_Hqz-5luk83lz7nynjZ4pcOtcpVtmlYJ6kvLl1eWCXo0wUbKKYXEBUpAMsYU2adYLIIV746un8SM7SjB0W9dhR8j9T_48L3x7-BgAA___FIoJu) (SPLC) on Tuesday on 11 counts. Attorney General Todd Blanche alleged the organization secretly paid Ku Klux Klan leaders and other hate group members as informants while raising millions off the threat those same groups posed to donors. The 11-count indictment spans wire fraud, false statements to a federally insured bank, and money laundering conspiracy. The [Department of Justice](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckDGu2zAQRE9DdTSolUzKBYs06n7alMKKXNmbUKRAri3k9oFyhN9NMZh5eL--li_kxPn5E3fyVbYllrgk2uTk_GxHCpwjB6EYaW91AQNWm1EDLDkt0EUfQ8Q-dOR75-zDmOFhupcfLQ3OwIqwut5O5h7HOEZ3x35b-95hx_6aMiMADGBhuj0QH9MQCKfobL9uajSYqMqt0vFeEwfMgu3PVmqgWyh7l_xL5Ghq-KFgVjCf53k7SmLhUK6CgjnT2RTM15OC2YxX7hXMrbzlRTXro3yoyl-d8NSBslDVv99NOJCOdGCVnbJozh9qwk8ULlkbM033wdmu-nicnBI369Ronjty-k8m3xD58fAvAAD__9i1gs4) (DOJ) says the SPLC publicly cast hate groups as existential threats to donors while quietly putting those same organizations on its payroll for intelligence. The SPLC called the prosecution [political weaponization](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L1urTAQBOCngc7ILP-Fi9vQndumRMZewybGRvZyUN4-Io-QbqSRPo3m47W8NHkK2399oErsFhvt4tHxTWHLpzcULBlGa_HIaQEJvZCtAFiCX6C0yhqra1Oiqoehn6RsJlnuyjnTj904tYNprB1cVzf1MJp-kusIbdeVpB5KtgDQQA9jNWk9jY1BPdqhr1dXtFJ7TFwlPK_Vk9GBdf5yMRmsTDxKr3bmMxfNvwLmAub7viuz5oB3fvoC5icWMOd48Y4piDO-MfG38PoWBgNjEp9XZjIoLJ468YGBBYU3ZqZNM8UgKLiYDh04i10zii3F63zUMil73uQ95X4oWrkdmvzvMP7Dj28FPwEAAP__i3SGmg), saying the Trump administration is targeting civil rights organizations. The indictment is the most aggressive action yet in the Trump DOJ's escalating campaign against left-leaning nonprofits. ★★★
Senate Advances $70B Immigration Bill

Senate Republicans voted 52-46 Tuesday on a strict party-line vote to open debate on a budget resolution that would push $70 billion in immigration enforcement through reconciliation, bypassing the Democratic filibuster. The vote, [reported by Roll Call](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLFu9CAQhJ8Gd5xg7R_sguJv3F3alNYerH3o1mABzr1-5OQN0s1opG-k7_O-3DFyTNsH7uRKW5eQw8K0tndMWz3YxxSibxQC7bUsoMBINUiAJfECXXDBB9S-I6etNZNS_aS6pwNtvdY0KA9BW0NWkRono_1o_4Ffxy66C6UGAOjBwHibEKex94RjsEY_VjEoZCrtVug4Hxw9pob1tebi6ebz3rF7tnZU0f8XMAuYS2b2yHyNAuYLL2BWw5W1gLlSwkYSt0JUZcuy4YvkecjHGTZqslDNfLaYk1xzkXHf41bwt58p1K64cLwjc6zGikFtO8afs679QdyXg-8AAAD__3GVfW4), unlocks up to 50 hours of debate and a vote-a-rama of unlimited amendments before a final passage vote. The measure would fund Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Customs and Border Protection (CBP), and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) through Trump's term. Passage would end [the longest partial shutdown](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLGStCAQhJ8GMywcXdGA4E_M9k8vtAYYXOoQLGCP17_ykssvnOmu_rr647k_0Qcfj_94ksrV7TbZPZCrzcejXMH4aL2pZC2dJe8gYOZi4gB7DDt0VlljcTAdqUHKeRViXEX3UlK4wRDSrHFdFynHZX24QWh0I8z64Tqv7igxAcAIMyz9irguoyFcrJwH7dgkMFCufabrrYM3GCuWT5eyod6kswvqVetV2PiPwcZga631DcvLx6OmWP1J5fYx2CK1wmC7gQw2vPJ9DAy2QhEr8V9C4ZoOH7klfQv6bQ-q_AoYuRRc-xB8ilynVCqDrcvKXu1-llmySRwn-vDTrf5hyi8F3wEAAP__0faEag) in U.S. history, which began after Democrats blocked DHS appropriations following a deadly ICE operation in Minneapolis. Republicans say they had no choice but to act unilaterally after months of Democratic stonewalling on DHS funding. Democrats say restoring DHS appropriations without accountability for the [Minneapolis deaths](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LGOpiAUBeCnwU6DVxaloNjG7t92S4P3ot4MoAH-8fUnTjP9dCc5yXeS8_-1vBwHTvs_F73NdVvopCX4rd6c9nIF5ESM1RP5WPICEnQrVQuwpLBAQ5aQXI-Nt_04aiPlYGRzWIWTnvQ0mHE0Pf4ho1YjURPhtmrjoWH7UFIBwAAaps44Z6YBvZto1P26CSVd8Ll22V_vNTC6VF352M6MvsMzNsEetV5FDH8FzALm-747TCs-pYD54QXMUj25FzAXn1z17Q9XWo6R9-wqn6mlo7TleFc679Qy-u6oMTTZ0nVzCFz0KJTco-PwvV5_cdanha8AAAD__xJ0eV4) is a non-starter, leaving the standoff heading into a chaotic amendment process.

# Happy Earth Day!
Adelita for Congress Newsletter
---
| | Hi Peter,

Happy Earth Day! 🌍 No one fights harder for our environment than Adelita. Whether it is fighting for clean air, safe water, **holding polluters and corporations accountable** , supporting scientific research, honoring indigenous sovereignty, or protecting public lands, we know **Adelita always has our backs.**
We also wanted to take this moment to share that**Sunrise Movement** , one of the leading **climate justice advocacy organizations** has decided to endorse our campaign!
_**Sunrise is building a movement** of young people to end billionaire rule and stop the climate crisis. Together, we will **disrupt business as usual** to force Donald Trump out of power. We’re on a mission to put everyday people back in charge and build a world that works for all of us, **now and for generations to come.**_
This endorsement is a **POWERFUL** one and demonstrates how committed Adelita is to fighting for the climate future **WE DESERVE!**
---

**Our movement is growing... BIG things are coming! 🤩** We’ll be launching new volunteer shifts soon- stay tuned to keep up with all the latest campaign news.

We’re always happy to have new faces, so if you know someone who would like to volunteer, **send them the link below** or they can [**scan and sign up**](https://adelitaforcongress.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=4efffbdef3b238a45f56f3bb2&id=3fe0edf6f5&e=f7c3700ccb)**** because we WILL need as many volunteers once it starts rolling! Let’s keep building our momentum for **Adelita, Southern Arizona’s biggest fighter!**

# Rep. Jasmine Clark Releases Statement on the Passing of Rep. David Scott
---
**LILBURN, GA** – Today, Rep. Dr. Jasmine Clark (D-Lilburn), a microbiologist, Emory University professor, and candidate for Congress, released a statement on the passing of Rep. David Scott: “Earlier today I received the heartbreaking news of the passing of Congressman David Scott. I am praying for Mrs. Alfredia Scott, their daughters Danya and Marcye, and their grandchildren, and all throughout our communities who loved him. His legacy of unwavering dedication to public service for more than fifty years will live on. From his job fairs, to his support of farmers, veterans, and HBCUs, and more, Congressman Scott’s impact is woven into the fabric of our community and will live on in Georgia’s story. Today we mourn his passing while also celebrating a life well lived. My heart is with all who are impacted. May they find strength and comfort in the days ahead.”

Hungarians voted out 16 years of autocracy. Here's what that means for us. |
#
---
Hey team, Last week, Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán — who has dominated his country’s politics for most of the last decade and a half — was ousted by voters turning out in the greatest numbers since the 1990s. He didn’t govern like a “small-d” democratic leader. He followed the authoritarian playbook step by step: stack the courts, rewrite the rules, seize the media, and use government power to reward loyalists and punish critics. Even the Cato Institute — a conservative, libertarian think tank — has documented how he undermined judicial independence, the separation of powers, and a free press to concentrate power in his own hands. As someone who has worn our nation’s uniform and served in war zones, I’ve seen what happens when strongmen hollow out democratic institutions. It doesn’t happen all at once. It happens one norm, one law, one independent voice at a time. What happened in Hungary serves as a warning of what could come if we stay on this path. Because we’re watching the same authoritarian playbook being tested in the United States: attacks on judges and prosecutors, efforts to intimidate the press, and the open promise to use the machinery of government to go after political enemies and protect allies. Orbán's Hungary is a cautionary tale for every American who believes in the rule of law. But cautionary tales can have hopeful endings — _**if people find the courage to show up.**_ That's what Hungarians did. Conservatives, progressives, independents, the disillusioned and the determined — they all showed up together. It didn’t happen in a single election cycle. It took years of painstaking work, organizing, listening, and coalition building. **In the end, democracy proved stronger than one man’s grip on power.** Now it’s our turn. We have a chance to build a broad, durable movement here at home — one that brings together working people from every background, puts country over party, and refuses to hand our institutions over to would-be strongmen. **That takes courage, humility, and a lot of hard work between elections, not just in the final weeks.** [**I’m asking you to stand with us today by donating to build the kind of people power that beat back authoritarianism abroad — and will defend our institutions here. But we also won’t ignore [**_fraud_**](https://links.email.lawlerforcongress.com/els/v4/l1tzg6lqrxafhwoikxric/YxOC2eSW5FhBvHyJkj9kFTdn0vM9zqe7Utur_W48H0xYemoIdWSAB39A57tnY7noDGRU/kDUPfhlAvIXzoUtBesimKN9ZNZ_B1r928nVwdqQIZapX0SzhEAP-6m5hLzXGlTCBbH4ojr4ObONHRr2eIAn4PTgiTUuP0VNlFEyBAoTc9JYbDQjntd3QSA5v_k3SF1VuBx6cNkOKbmExanbMIUNzwkjrmAoKnbIqidIlDhC0bhEwv0FnvKXPHWieYhplXDvCDin6qntvZyd4F2S5wnap0CGRa2ACiIPrnk2QUnfknc6xHilNM1mcB65WFmNpkcKLtquU-kbvQno=) when we see it.

That’s not how New York law works.
When fraud permeates a petition, the entire petition is thrown out.
Not part of it.
All of it.
Our legal filing laid out what we found:
— Thirty sworn voter affidavits reporting forged signatures
— Witness testimony identifying fraud across multiple canvassers

This isn’t politics.

Legal fights like this aren’t optional once fraud is uncovered.
But they are expensive.
If you believe election fraud should never be tolerated — no matter who commits it — we’re asking for your help to support this legal fight.

[_**But today, I want to make the case why your support of my campaign is so important to our climate movement.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129982926/616214739/-1071876423?&refcode=E29303-20260422-EarthDay-SL-EnvironmentClimate&amount=5&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDMxMTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZjlkZmNkY2ItYTUzZS1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=a77vhkPYDKMX3assPVQdl_34sVp1wSdUn2syFrVbUUc=) Look, Peter: I’ve always been vocal about the reality of climate change. It’s why I’m so concerned about the Trump administration’s efforts to fire scientists and let big polluters off the hook by gutting clean air standards. I’ve also been one of the loudest voices in Congress on the frontlines of our wildfire crisis. We must take immediate action to make our communities more fire resilient. That starts with supporting the heroes on the ground. I fought to give our firefighters the pay raise they deserve for battling extreme conditions to protect our homes and keep us safe. The 2026 election is a turning point for our planet. The science is clear: we have a very narrow window to reduce our carbon emissions and prevent the worst effects of climate change for future generations. My race in California’s 9th district is a must-win. We cannot let MAGA extremists flip this seat, or we lose our ability to fight back against Trump’s attacks on our environment and make real progress. The 2026 election is a turning point for our planet.
